definition_zh: 使娱乐；招待；怀有（想法）
definition_en: to amuse people, to receive guests, or to keep an idea in mind
core_image: 主人张开双臂把客人迎进屋，让他们坐下、吃喝、笑出声
scene: 晚饭后爷爷讲了一个长笑话，把孩子们逗得直笑。 Grandpa told a long joke after dinner and entertained the children for an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 entertain 是「使娱乐」（第 1 个义项：让人开心消遣）；句意：晚饭后爷爷讲了一个长笑话，逗得孩子们笑了一个小时。

senses.title: To amuse and hold attention
senses.definition: to give people pleasure and keep them interested
senses.definitionCN: 给人快乐并让他们保持兴趣
senses.example: The clown entertained the crowd for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 小丑逗了观众一个小时。
senses.why: The old sense of holding someone is applied to holding their attention pleasantly.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「留住某人」之意，被用来表示愉快地留住他们的注意力。

senses.title: To receive guests
senses.definition: to welcome guests and provide food, drink, or company
senses.definitionCN: 迎接客人并提供饮食或陪伴
senses.example: They entertained friends at home all weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 整个周末他们都在家招待朋友。
senses.why: Hospitality is the oldest social sense: keeping people together in your house.
senses.whyCN: 待客是最古老的社交义项：把人们留在自己家里相聚。

senses.title: To hold an idea in mind
senses.definition: to consider or keep an idea, hope, or doubt in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在心里考虑或保留某种想法、希望或疑虑
senses.example: He refused to entertain the idea of moving abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝考虑移居国外的想法。
senses.why: The mind is pictured as a host that can receive and hold a thought.
senses.whyCN: 心智被想象成一位可以接纳并留住想法的主人。

intro.en: Entertain comes from Old French entretenir, to hold together or maintain, from entre, between, and tenir, to hold.
intro.cn: entertain 来自古法语 entretenir（使相聚、维持），由 entre（之间）与 tenir（握住）构成。

items.en: Tenere means to hold or keep.
items.cn: tenere 意为握住、保持。

items.en: Tenir continues the Latin verb for holding.
items.cn: tenir 延续拉丁语中表示「握住」的动词。

items.en: Entretenir means to hold together and keep up.
items.cn: entretenir 意为使相聚、维持。

items.en: Middle English entretinen means to keep up or maintain.
items.cn: 中古英语 entretinen 意为维持、保持。

items.en: The sense of amusing guests and audiences becomes common.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，招待客人、娱乐观众的意思流行起来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the amusement, hospitality, and mental senses together.
items.cn: 现代英语把娱乐、招待与心中怀有三个义项并存。

note.en: Entertain is a holding verb, and it sits near its own family and near words for amusing and hosting.
note.cn: entertain 是一个「留住」动词，与自身词族以及表示逗乐和待客的词相邻。

entries.definition: shows or activities that amuse people
a person who amuses an audience
amusing and enjoyable
to make someone laugh or smile
to receive and look after guests
to keep a thought or feeling in mind

normalIntro.en: Entertain goes back to French tenir, to hold: it holds a guest's attention and keeps it.
normalIntro.cn: entertain 可追溯到法语 tenir（握住）：它把客人的注意力握住并留住。

normal.en: Enter- means between, and tenir means hold: to hold someone in a pleasant state.
normal.cn: enter- 表示之间，tenir 表示握住：把某人留在愉快的状态里。

normal.en: Entertain guests is the older hospitality sense.
normal.cn: entertain guests 是更古老的待客义项。

normal.en: Entertain an idea is to hold it in the mind for a while.
normal.cn: entertain an idea 是把想法在心里留一会儿。

normal.en: Entertainment is the noun, and entertainer is the person.
normal.cn: entertainment 是名词，entertainer 是人。

normal.en: Compare amuse: amuse makes people laugh, while entertain can also mean to host.
normal.cn: 对比 amuse：amuse 让人发笑，而 entertain 还可表示招待。

abstract.en: Picture a host holding open the door while plates are passed around.
abstract.cn: 想象主人扶着门，盘子在客人之间传递。

abstract.en: Imagine a juggler keeping five balls in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象杂耍者让五个球停在空中。

abstract.en: Think of a thought held lightly in the palm before it is accepted.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法被轻轻托在掌心，尚未被接受。

examples.en: The clown entertained the crowd for an hour.
examples.cn: 小丑逗了观众一个小时。

examples.en: They entertained friends at home all weekend.
examples.cn: 整个周末他们都在家招待朋友。

examples.en: He refused to entertain the idea of moving abroad.
examples.cn: 他拒绝考虑移居国外的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enter + ten」——把客人请进门，再用十成的热情留住他，就是招待与娱乐；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tenere（握住）→ 古法语 entretenir（维持、使相聚）→ 中古英语 entretinen → 现代英语 entertain，由「留住、维持」引申为招待与娱乐。

sensesIntro.en: The verb first means to keep something together, then to keep guests, then to keep attention amused, and finally to keep an idea in mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词先表示「维持在一起」，再表示留住客人，继而表示留住注意力使人开心，最后表示把想法留在心里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: guests held in a warm circle of food, talk, and laughter.
core.cn: 核心意象：客人被留在饮食、交谈与笑声组成的温暖圈子里。

branches.en: Amusing people is holding their attention pleasantly.
branches.cn: 逗人开心，就是愉快地留住注意力。

branches.en: Hospitality keeps guests physically and socially close.
branches.cn: 待客让客人在身体与社交上保持亲近。

branches.en: Holding an idea keeps it in the mind as a guest.
branches.cn: 怀有想法，就是把它当作客人留在心里。

branches.en: A good host both feeds guests and keeps them amused.
branches.cn: 好主人既招待饮食，也让客人开心。

branches.en: Receiving people and receiving ideas both use the same holding image.
branches.cn: 接纳人与接纳想法使用同一个「留住」意象。

intro.en: Entertain is a French verb rebuilt on a Latin root, and English endings carry it into noun and adjective forms.
intro.cn: entertain 是建立在拉丁词根上的法语动词，英语词尾把它扩展到名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere means to hold, and French entretenir means to hold together or keep up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere 表示握住，法语 entretenir 表示使相聚、维持。

items.exampleCN: entre- 出现在 entretenir 开头。

items.example: Inter is the Latin source of entre-.
items.exampleCN: inter 是 entre- 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Tenere is the deep root of tenir.
items.exampleCN: tenere 是 tenir 的深层词根。

items.example: Entretenir joins the prefix and the verb.
items.exampleCN: entretenir 把前缀与动词结合。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

items.example: Entertainment is what the verb produces.
items.exampleCN: entertainment 是动词产生的结果。

items.example: Entertainer names the person on stage.
items.exampleCN: entertainer 指舞台上的那个人。

definition_zh: 等级制度；层级体系；统治集团；阶层
definition_en: a system in which people or things are arranged in ranks, with each level ranking above or below another
core_image: 一座一级一级向上收窄的金字塔，每层只对紧挨着的上一层负责
scene: 这里指「等级制度」。 In the hospital, a strict hierarchy decides who may overrule whom during an emergency.
sceneCN: 这里 hierarchy 是「等级体系」（第 1 个义项：组织内部按上下级排列的层级结构）；句意：在医院里，一套严格的等级体系决定紧急情况下谁可以否决谁。场景要点：手术台旁不同颜色的工牌、由下向上的汇报链、每一层只对紧挨着的上一层负责。

pos.zh: 等级制度；层级体系；阶层
（生物学）分类层级；（计算机）层次结构

derivatives.zh: 等级制的；按等级划分的
等级体系中的高层人物；高级教士
等级体系的（较少用变体）

senses.title: A ranked organisation of people
senses.definition: a system in which people or positions are arranged in ranks, so that each rank has authority over the one below it
senses.definitionCN: 把人或职位按等级排列的体系，每一级对下一级拥有权威
senses.example: The firm's hierarchy puts every decision through three levels of approval.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的等级体系让每项决定都要经过三层审批。
senses.why: The core image is a pyramid that narrows as it rises: each level holds authority over the level beneath it, and the shape of the whole depends on that step-by-step arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一座向上收窄的金字塔：每一级对下面一级拥有权威，整体的形状就取决于这种逐级排列。

senses.title: A ranking by importance
senses.definition: an ordering of things from most to least important, powerful, or urgent
senses.definitionCN: 按重要、强大或紧急程度从高到低排列的顺序
senses.example: The report sets out a hierarchy of risks, from flooding to noise.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了一个风险层级，从洪水一直到噪音。
senses.why: The pyramid can also be built from things rather than people: what sits near the top matters more, and what sits below can wait. The vertical order becomes a scale of value.
senses.whyCN: 这座金字塔也可以由事物而不是人来搭建：靠近顶端的更重要，下面的可以等。垂直顺序由此变成价值尺度。

senses.title: The ruling group at the top
senses.definition: the small group of people who hold the highest positions and control an organisation or society
senses.definitionCN: 占据最高位置、控制某一组织或社会的一小群人
senses.example: Reform was blocked by the party hierarchy.
senses.exampleCN: 改革被党的上层集团阻挠了。
senses.why: By a common shift, the name of the structure comes to mean the people at its narrow top. The pyramid is reduced to its peak, and 'the hierarchy' becomes 'those who decide'.
senses.whyCN: 一种常见的转喻：结构的名称变成了结构顶端那一小群人。金字塔被缩减为塔尖，the hierarchy 也就成了“决定者”。

senses.title: Biological classification ranks
senses.definition: the nested series of categories used to classify organisms, from kingdom down to species
senses.definitionCN: 用于对生物分类的一整套嵌套范畴，从界一直到种
senses.example: Linnaeus arranged living things in a hierarchy of kingdom, class, order, genus and species.
senses.exampleCN: 林奈把生物安排进界、纲、目、属、种这样的层级中。
senses.why: Taxonomy is a pyramid of sets: each rank contains the ranks below it, so a species sits inside a genus, a genus inside a family. The word's vertical shape fits nested classification exactly.
senses.whyCN: 分类学是一个集合的金字塔：每一级都包含下面几级，所以种在属内，属在科内。这个词的垂直形状恰好适合嵌套分类。

senses.title: A layered structure in computing
senses.definition: an arrangement of files, data, or system layers in which each level is contained in or depends on the level above
senses.definitionCN: 文件、数据或系统层次的安排方式，每一层被上一层包含或依赖上一层
senses.example: The folder hierarchy puts every image under its project year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个文件夹层级把每张图片放在对应的项目年份之下。
senses.why: A file tree is a pyramid drawn sideways: one root, branching levels, each item belonging to exactly one parent. The social image survives as containment and dependence rather than authority.
senses.whyCN: 文件树是把金字塔横着画：一个根、逐层分支、每一项只属于一个父项。社会意象在这里保存为包含与依赖，而不是权威。

senses.title: The nine orders of angels
senses.titleCN: 天使九阶：最初的神学义
senses.definition: in Christian theology, the ranked divisions of angels described by Dionysius the Areopagite; the word's earliest English sense
senses.definitionCN: 基督教神学中由伪丢尼修描述的天使等级划分；这是该词最早的英语义项
senses.example: Medieval writers mapped the nine angelic hierarchy onto the nine spheres of heaven.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪作家把天使九阶对应到九重天球上。
senses.why: The word entered English in the late 14th century as a name for the sacred order of angels. Its first hierarchy was not a company but a cosmos: ranks of being, each closer to the divine than the one below.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 14 世纪晚期进入英语时，是天使神圣秩序的名称。它最初的层级不是公司，而是宇宙：存在的等级，每一级都比下一级更接近神。

senses.title: The order of the clergy
senses.definition: the ranked order of clergy, from deacon and priest up to bishop and pope
senses.definitionCN: 神职人员的等级秩序，从执事、司铎一直向上到主教与教宗
senses.example: A bishop's place in the hierarchy was fixed by canon law.
senses.exampleCN: 主教在教阶体系中的位置由教会法规定。
senses.why: The Greek source means 'rule of a high priest', so the church is where the word feels most at home. Each rank holds sacred office over the rank below, and the ladder runs up to a single summit.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头意为“大祭司的统治”，因此教会是这个词最如鱼得水的地方。每一级对下一级拥有圣职权威，阶梯一直通向唯一的顶端。

senses.title: A hierarchy of knowledge or values
senses.definition: an abstract ordering in which ideas, laws, or values are ranked as more fundamental than others
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、法律或价值按根本程度排列的抽象秩序
senses.example: In legal theory, the constitution sits at the top of a hierarchy of norms.
senses.exampleCN: 在法律理论中，宪法位于规范层级的顶端。
senses.why: Once the image is abstract, anything that can be 'higher' or 'lower' in rank can form a hierarchy: norms, needs, genres, values. The pyramid becomes a way of saying that some things rest on others.
senses.whyCN: 一旦意象抽象化，任何能在等级上分“高下”的东西都能构成 hierarchy：规范、需求、文类、价值。金字塔变成一种说法，表示某些事物依托于另一些事物。

intro.en: Hierarchy began as a word for the ranks of angels, built from Greek words for 'sacred' and 'rule'. Its modern organisational sense is much later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hierarchy 最初是天使等级的名称，由希腊语“神圣”与“统治”两个词构成。它现代的组织义要晚得多。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as jerarchie / ierarchie, meaning 'rank in the sacred order' and 'one of the three divisions of the nine orders of angels'; loosely also 'rule, dominion'.
items.cn: 最早以 jerarchie／ierarchie 记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“神圣秩序中的等级”以及“天使九阶中三大划分之一”；宽泛地也指“统治、管辖”。

items.en: From Old French ierarchie (14c., Modern French hiérarchie), from Medieval Latin hierarchia 'ranked division of angels', the system of Dionysius the Areopagite.
items.cn: 来自古法语 ierarchie（14 世纪，现代法语 hiérarchie），再来自中世纪拉丁语 hierarchia“天使的等级划分”，即伪丢尼修的体系。

items.en: Greek hierarkhia meant 'rule of a high priest', from hierarkhēs 'high priest, leader of sacred rites': ta hiera 'the sacred rites' (from hieros 'sacred') plus arkhein 'to lead, rule'.
items.cn: 希腊语 hierarkhia 意为“大祭司的统治”，来自 hierarkhēs“大祭司、圣礼的主持者”：ta hiera“圣礼”（出自 hieros“神圣”）加 arkhein“引领、统治”。

items.en: The sense 'ranked organisation of persons or things' is recorded in English by the 1610s, at first of the clergy. It was probably reinforced by the unrelated English word higher, which sounds like the start of hierarchy.
items.cn: “人或事物的等级组织”这一义项在 17 世纪 10 年代有记录，最初用于神职人员。它很可能被无关的英语词 higher 强化，因为 higher 听起来像 hierarchy 的开头。

items.en: The word extends to secular institutions, then to natural classification. Taxonomy, army ranks and civil service grades all become hierarchies in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到世俗机构，再扩展到自然分类。分类学、军衔与文官等级在日常语言中都成了 hierarchy。

items.en: Management theory, linguistics and computing adopt it: chain of command, syntactic hierarchy, folder hierarchy. The Greek sacred order becomes a general model of layered structure.
items.cn: 管理学、语言学与计算机科学采用它：指挥链、句法层级、文件夹层级。希腊的神圣秩序变成了分层结构的一般模型。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective and person forms, and warns about the unrelated word higher; the second group compares ways of ordering people and things.
note.cn: 第一组把名词与它的形容词、指人形式分开，并提醒注意无关的 higher；第二组比较排列人与事物的不同说法。

entries.definition: arranged in ranks, or organised by levels of authority. It describes the shape; hierarchy is the shape itself.
entries.definitionCN: 按等级排列的，或按权威层级组织的。它描述形状；hierarchy 是形状本身。

entries.definition: a person at the top of a hierarchy, especially a senior cleric. It names one holder of rank, not the system of ranks.
entries.definitionCN: 等级体系顶端的人，尤指高级教士。它命名一位占据等级的人，而不是等级体系。

entries.definition: an uncommon variant of hierarchical. It is best avoided when hierarchical is available, since the two are easily confused in writing.
entries.definitionCN: hierarchical 的不常见变体。既然有 hierarchical，最好避免使用，因为两者在书面上极易混淆。

entries.definition: the comparative of high. It is not related to hierarchy, though its sound probably helped the modern sense of ranked organisation take hold.
entries.definitionCN: high 的比较级。它与 hierarchy 没有词源关系，但它的读音很可能帮助了现代“等级组织”义项扎根。

entries.definition: a single level or position in an order. Rank is one rung; hierarchy is the whole ladder and the rule that connects its rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 秩序中的单个级别或位置。rank 是一级横档；hierarchy 是整架梯子以及连接各横档的规则。

entries.definition: the way things are arranged, or a sequence. Order can be flat and neutral, like alphabetical order; hierarchy always implies higher and lower.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被安排的方式，或序列。order 可以是平铺中性的，如字母顺序；hierarchy 总含高下之分。

entries.definition: the informal ranking of status within a group, originally observed in hens. It is vivid and colloquial; hierarchy is neutral and structural.
entries.definitionCN: 群体内部非正式的位次排序，最初来自对鸡群的观察。它形象而口语化；hierarchy 中性且结构化。

entries.definition: the line through which orders pass from superior to subordinate. It stresses communication and obedience, while hierarchy stresses the whole ranked structure.
entries.definitionCN: 命令由上级传到下级的线路。它强调传达与服从，hierarchy 则强调整个等级结构。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek hieros 'sacred' plus arkhein 'to rule', and the arch- family that still marks rule in English.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 hieros“神圣”加 arkhein“统治”，以及英语中仍标记“统治”的 arch- 词族。

normal.en: Hierarchy literally joins 'sacred' and 'rule': its first home was the order of angels, not the office org chart.
normal.cn: hierarchy 字面上把“神圣”与“统治”连在一起：它最初的家是天使的秩序，而不是办公室的组织图。

normal.en: The arch- in hierarchy is the same arch- that rules in monarchy, anarchy and patriarch: arkhein means 'to lead, rule'.
normal.cn: hierarchy 里的 arch- 与 monarchy、anarchy、patriarch 中表示统治的 arch- 相同：arkhein 意为“引领、统治”。

normal.en: Hierarchy and higher are not related. The resemblance is a coincidence that probably helped the modern meaning feel natural.
normal.cn: hierarchy 与 higher 没有词源关系。这种相似是巧合，但它很可能让现代词义显得更自然。

normal.en: A hierarchy of needs is a real fixed phrase from psychology: needs are stacked, with basic ones below and refined ones above.
normal.cn: hierarchy of needs 是心理学中真实的固定说法：需求被堆叠起来，基本需求在下，精致需求在上。

normal.en: In computing, a folder hierarchy is a tree: one root, many branches, every item with exactly one parent.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，文件夹层级是一棵树：一个根、许多分支，每一项只有一个父项。

abstract.en: Picture a pyramid of stone steps: the base is wide, the top is narrow, and each step exists only because the one below holds it up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座石阶金字塔：底部宽，顶端窄，每一级之所以存在，是因为下面一级托着它。

abstract.en: The same pyramid can be made of people, ranks, species, files or values. What stays constant is that some things rest on others and none may float.
abstract.cn: 同一座金字塔可以由人、军衔、物种、文件或价值搭成。不变的是：某些事物依托于另一些事物，没有谁能悬空。

abstract.en: When people say 'the hierarchy', they mean the narrow top of the pyramid: the structure has shrunk to the few who decide.
abstract.cn: 当人们说 the hierarchy，指的是金字塔狭窄的顶端：整个结构被缩减为少数做决定的人。

examples.en: The old monastery kept a hierarchy so precise that even the order of seating was recorded.
examples.cn: 那座古老修道院的等级秩序精确到连座次都被记录下来。

examples.en: Flat teams often claim to have no hierarchy, yet informal rankings reappear within weeks.
examples.cn: 扁平化团队常声称没有等级，但非正式的位次几周内就会重新出现。

examples.en: The database stores every page in a hierarchy of folders rather than a single list.
examples.cn: 这个数据库把每个页面存放在文件夹层级中，而不是一张单层列表里。

dict_mnemonic.text: “海尔拉基”——海尔把员工拉成一级一级的基座，越往上人越少 → hierarchy 等级制度

root: 源自希腊语 hierarkhia“大祭司的统治”，由 hieros“神圣”+ arkhein“统治”构成，核心是“按等级层层向上、每层对下层拥有权威”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of hierarchy, all grown from one shape: a pyramid of ranks in which each level rests on the one below and answers to the one above.
sensesIntro.cn: hierarchy 的八个义项都从同一个形状长出来：一座等级金字塔，每一级依托下一级，并向上一级负责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrowing pyramid of ranks, each level resting on the one below and answering to the one above.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座逐级收窄的等级金字塔，每层依托下层，并对上层负责。

branches.en: ORGANISATION AND POWER: a ranked body of people, and then the narrow group at its top who actually decide.
branches.cn: 组织与权力：先是按等级排列的人群，再是位于塔尖、真正做决定的那一小群。

branches.en: ORDERING: the same vertical shape ranks risks, needs, norms and values by importance or fundamentality.
branches.cn: 排序：同一垂直形状按重要性或根本性排列风险、需求、规范与价值。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: nested sets reproduce the pyramid exactly, since each taxonomic rank contains the ranks below it.
branches.cn: 生物学：嵌套集合精确复制了金字塔，因为每个分类层级都包含下面几级。

branches.en: COMPUTING: a tree is the pyramid laid on its side, with containment and dependency instead of obedience.
branches.cn: 计算机：树是横放的金字塔，用包含与依赖替代了服从。

branches.en: THE SACRED SOURCE: angels and clergy are the word's first home, where rank means proximity to the divine.
branches.cn: 神圣源头：天使与神职人员是这个词最初的家，等级意味着与神更近。

intro.en: Hierarchy is a Greek compound borrowed through Latin and French: hieros 'sacred' + arkhein 'to rule'. English adds -al, -ic, -ically and -arch to the same stem.
intro.cn: hierarchy 是经拉丁语和法语借入的希腊语复合词：hieros“神圣”+ arkhein“统治”。英语在同一词干上加 -al、-ic、-ically 与 -arch。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin hierarchia and hierarcha carried the Greek word into church writing. The second element, arkhein, is the source of the productive English combining form -arch, meaning 'ruler'.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 hierarchia 与 hierarcha 把这个希腊词带进教会写作。第二个成分 arkhein 是英语能产后缀 -arch（意为“统治者”）的来源。

items.meaningCN: 等级制的；按层级划分的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: The archive uses a hierarchical system of folders.
items.exampleCN: 这个档案库使用层级化的文件夹系统。

items.meaning: of or relating to a hierarchy
items.meaningCN: 等级体系的；层级式的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The diagram shows the hierarchic links between teams.
items.exampleCN: 这张图显示各团队之间的层级联系。

items.meaning: a chief ruler in sacred matters; a high-ranking member of a hierarchy
items.meaningCN: 高级教士；等级体系中的高层人物
items.example: The hierarch blessed the new chapel.
items.exampleCN: 这位高级教士为新礼拜堂祝圣。

items.meaning: in a ranked or layered way
items.example: The data is organised hierarchically, from region to street.
items.exampleCN: 数据按层级组织，从大区一直到街道。

items.meaningCN: 等级体系的（较少使用的形容词变体）
items.example: Older texts prefer hierarchal to hierarchical.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本更爱用 hierarchal 而不是 hierarchical。

items.meaningCN: 君主制；一人统治（mono- 单一 + -archy 统治）
items.example: The monarchy survived the revolution in a ceremonial form.
items.exampleCN: 君主制以礼仪形式在革命后存续下来。

items.meaning: a state without government or order
items.meaningCN: 无政府状态；混乱（an- 无 + -archy 统治）
items.example: The power cut left the station in near anarchy.
items.exampleCN: 停电让车站几乎陷入无秩序状态。

items.example: The company drifted into an oligarchy of three directors.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司逐渐变成三位董事的寡头统治。

items.meaning: the male head of a family or church
items.meaningCN: 家长；宗主教（patri- 父 + -arch 统治者）
items.exampleCN: 宗主教带领了游行队伍。

items.meaning: a bishop of the highest rank
a chief magistrate in ancient Athens
items.example: The archon was chosen by lot each year.
items.exampleCN: 执政官每年以抽签方式选出。

latinEntries.structure: Greek hierarkhia, borrowed into Medieval Latin
latinEntries.meaning: the ranked division of angels; sacred rule
latinEntries.meaningCN: 天使的等级划分；神圣统治

latinEntries.meaning: a high priest, one who rules in sacred things

definition_zh: 使最大化；使增至最大；充分利用；把……发挥到极致
definition_en: to make something as great, large, or effective as it can possibly be
core_image: 把一只旋钮拧到刻度盘最右端、直到再也拧不动的顶点
scene: 这里指「使最大化」。 The plant manager turned every dial to its limit to maximize output before the export deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 maximize 是「把产量推到最高」（第 3 个义项：把产出、效率推到最高）；句意：出口截止日前，厂长把每一个旋钮都拧到极限，以把产量推到最高。场景要点：车间里的控制台、一排拧到头的旋钮、堆到天花板的成品箱。

pos.zh: 充分利用；把……发挥到极致

collocations.zh: 把成功的机会做到最大

derivatives.zh: 最大值；最大限度；最大的
最大的；达到最大限度的
追求最大化的人；最大化者
达到最高水平；最大值；最大的（口语缩略）

senses.title: Reach the mathematical maximum
senses.definition: to find or reach the highest value of a function, quantity, or variable
senses.definitionCN: 求取或达到函数、数量、变量的最高值
senses.example: To maximize the function, set its derivative to zero.
senses.exampleCN: 要使这个函数取最大值，把它的导数设为零。
senses.why: Latin maximus names the top point of a scale. The verb makes an object arrive at that point, so the mathematical sense is the image in its plainest form.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maximus 指刻度上的顶点。这个动词让对象抵达那个点，因此数学义是这幅意象最朴素的形态。

senses.title: Profit: make the return as large as possible
senses.definition: to make profit, revenue, or financial return as large as the situation allows
senses.definitionCN: 在条件允许的范围内把利润、收入或财务回报做到最大
senses.example: The firm cut staff and raised prices to maximize profit.
senses.exampleCN: 公司裁减员工并提高价格，以使利润最大化。
senses.why: Profit is a quantity on a dial. Turning that dial to the right end is the business version of the same gesture, and it is the sense that dominates business writing.
senses.whyCN: 利润是刻度盘上的一个量。把这只旋钮拧到最右端，就是同一个动作在商业里的版本，也是商业写作中最常见的义项。

senses.title: Output and efficiency: run everything at full capacity
senses.definition: to make production or efficiency as high as the equipment and time allow
senses.definitionCN: 在设备与时间允许的范围内把产量或效率做到最高
senses.example: The mill maximized output by running three shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂实行三班倒，把产量推到最高。
senses.why: Output is what a machine yields. Maximizing it means no capacity is left unused, so the top of the scale is also the point of full employment.
senses.whyCN: 产量是机器产出的东西。把它最大化，意味着没有一寸产能被闲置，因此刻度的顶点也是“全部投入使用”的那一点。

senses.title: Impact and effect: make it land as hard as possible
senses.titleCN: 影响与效果：让冲击达到最远
senses.definition: to make the effect or influence of something as strong and wide as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物的效果或影响力做到最强、最广
senses.example: The campaign was designed to maximize its impact on young voters.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动旨在把对年轻选民的影响做到最大。
senses.why: Effect is a force that travels. Pushing it to its greatest reach applies the same top-of-scale image to influence rather than to a number.
senses.whyCN: 效果是一种会传播的力量。把它推到最远的射程，就是把同一个“刻度到顶”的意象用在影响力上，而不是用在数字上。

senses.title: Chance and probability: make the odds as good as possible
senses.titleCN: 机会与概率：把胜算做到最大
senses.definition: to make the likelihood of a desired result as high as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把期望结果出现的可能性做到最高
senses.example: Apply early to maximize your chance of getting a place.
senses.exampleCN: 尽早申请，以把获得名额的机会做到最大。
senses.why: Probability is a number between zero and one. Maximizing it moves that number toward one, the upper end of its own small scale.
senses.whyCN: 概率是零到一之间的数。最大化就是把这个数推向一，也就是它自己那一小段刻度的上端。

senses.title: Use resources fully: leave nothing idle
senses.titleCN: 利用资源：不让任何一份闲置
senses.definition: to use a resource, space, or opportunity as fully as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把资源、空间或机会尽可能充分地用尽
senses.example: The new timetable maximizes the use of the existing trains.
senses.exampleCN: 新的时刻表把现有列车的利用率做到最高。
senses.why: A resource has a capacity. Maximizing means every unit of it is put to work, so the scale is measured in unused capacity rather than in output.
senses.whyCN: 资源有容量。最大化意味着它的每一个单位都被投入使用，因此这把尺子量的是“还剩多少没用”，而不是产量。

senses.title: Computing: enlarge a window to fill the screen
senses.titleCN: 计算机：把窗口放到满屏
senses.definition: to enlarge a window on a screen until it fills the available display area
senses.definitionCN: 把屏幕上的窗口放大到占满可用的显示区域
senses.example: Double-click the title bar to maximize the window.
senses.exampleCN: 双击标题栏即可把窗口最大化。
senses.why: A window has a size scale whose ceiling is the screen. The command drives the window to that ceiling, making the metaphor visible as a button.
senses.whyCN: 窗口有一个尺寸刻度，它的天花板就是屏幕。这个命令把窗口推到那层天花板，让比喻变成了一个可见的按钮。

senses.title: Biology: make fitness as high as possible
senses.titleCN: 生物学：把适应度推到最高
senses.definition: in evolutionary biology, to increase reproductive fitness to the highest level available in an environment
senses.definitionCN: 在演化生物学中，把繁殖适应度提高到环境所允许的最高水平
senses.example: Natural selection maximizes fitness in a given environment.
senses.exampleCN: 自然选择会把适应度在特定环境中推到最高。
senses.why: Evolutionary fitness is a score attached to a trait. Selection pushes that score toward its highest attainable value, exactly as a dial is turned to its stop.
senses.whyCN: 演化适应度是附在某个性状上的分数。选择把这个分数推向可达到的最高值，正像把旋钮拧到它的止点。

senses.title: Push a feature to an extreme, often at a cost
senses.titleCN: 把某一特征推到极端，往往付出代价
senses.definition: to make one feature or quantity as extreme as possible, usually by sacrificing something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某一特征或数量做到尽可能极端，通常以牺牲其他方面为代价
senses.example: The design maximizes contrast and ignores comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计把对比度做到最大，却不顾舒适度。
senses.why: When one quantity is driven to its top, everything else is subordinated to it. The word then carries a warning about single-minded extremes.
senses.whyCN: 当一个量被推到顶端，其他一切都得服从它。于是这个词带上了一层警告：只顾一头的极端做法。

intro.en: Maximize is a transparent English coinage of 1802, built on maximum plus -ize; the Latin pieces behind maximum are well documented. Dates are those given by standard etymological references.
intro.cn: maximize 是 1802 年由英语自造的词，构词清楚：maximum 加 -ize；maximum 背后的拉丁语成分有明确记载。年代采用通行词源资料给出的说法。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'to make as great as possible, raise to the highest degree'. It is an English formation from maximum + -ize, and Bentham is the first attested user.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 1802 年，意为“使尽可能大、提高到最高程度”。它是由 maximum 加 -ize 构成的英语自造词，边沁是最早可考的使用者。

items.en: Maximum entered English from French maximum and directly from Latin maximum, the neuter form of maximus 'greatest'. The noun supplied the base for the later verb.
items.cn: maximum 于 1740 年经法语 maximum 并直接由拉丁语 maximum 进入英语，后者是 maximus“最大的”的中性形式。这个名词为后来的动词提供了词基。

items.en: Latin maximus is the superlative of magnus 'great, large, big', and it belongs to the same scale as minor and minimus at the other end.
items.cn: 拉丁语 maximus 是 magnus“大的、巨大的”的最高级，它与另一端的 minor、minimus 同属一把尺子。

items.en: Maximus goes back to PIE *mag-samo-, the superlative form of *meg- 'great', the root also behind magnify, magnitude and magnate.
items.cn: maximus 可追溯到原始印欧语 *mag-samo-，即 *meg-“大”的最高级形式；该词根也是 magnify、magnitude、magnate 的来源。

items.en: Jeremy Bentham used maximize repeatedly in his utilitarian writing. The twin minimize is recorded in the same year and with the same author, so the two verbs were coined as a matching pair.
items.cn: 杰里米·边沁在功利主义写作中反复使用 maximize。与之配对的 minimize 记录于同一年、同样出自他手，因此这两个动词是一套成对造出来的。

items.en: British spelling is maximise. Maximization, maximizer and the clipped max (as a verb by 1986) complete the family. Maximize is an English verb, not a Latin one, even though every part of it looks Latin.
items.cn: 英式拼写为 maximise。maximization、maximizer 以及缩略的 max（1986 年起作动词）补足了词族。maximize 是英语动词而非拉丁语动词，尽管它的每个部件看起来都像拉丁语。

note.en: The first group separates the noun, the derived noun, the clipping and a look-alike with a different origin. The second group compares maximize with optimize, with plain increase, and with its two opposite poles, minimize and minimum.
note.cn: 第一组区分名词、派生名词、缩略词以及一个来源不同的形近词；第二组把 maximize 与 optimize、普通的 increase，以及它的两个对立端点 minimize、minimum 作比较。

entries.definition: the greatest amount or degree possible. It is the noun that maximize was built from, not a synonym of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最大数量或程度。它是构成 maximize 的名词词基，而不是这个动词的同义词。

entries.definition: a short statement of a general truth or rule of conduct, from Latin maxima propositio. It looks like maximum but belongs to a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 关于普遍真理或行为准则的简短格言，来自拉丁语 maxima propositio。它形似 maximum，却是另一个名词。

entries.definition: the act or process of maximizing. It names the process, while maximum names the end point.
entries.definitionCN: 最大化的行为或过程。它命名过程，而 maximum 命名终点。

entries.definition: informal short form of maximum, and by 1986 a verb meaning 'to reach the maximum level'. It is a clipping, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: maximum 的口语缩略形式，1986 年起也作动词，意为“达到最高水平”。它是缩略形式，不是另一条词根。

entries.definition: to make the best possible arrangement within given limits. It looks for the best compromise among competing factors, while maximize pushes one quantity to its ceiling.
entries.definitionCN: 在既定限制内做出尽可能好的安排。它在多个相互竞争的因素之间寻找最佳折中，而 maximize 把一个量推到它的天花板。

entries.definition: to make larger in amount. It says nothing about a ceiling: you can increase a number without ever reaching its maximum.
entries.definitionCN: 使数量变大。它不涉及天花板：你可以让一个数变大，却始终没到它的最大值。

entries.definition: to reduce to the smallest possible amount. It is the exact opposite pole: one verb turns the dial to the right, the other to the left.
entries.definitionCN: 使降到尽可能小的量。它正是对立的那一端：一个动词把旋钮向右拧，另一个向左拧。

entries.definition: the smallest amount or degree possible. It is the floor of the same scale whose ceiling is maximum.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最小数量或程度。它是同一把尺子的底端，而 maximum 是顶端。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maximum + -ize, the Latin superlative maximus, the magnus family, and the matched pair maximize / minimize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：maximum 加 -ize、拉丁最高级 maximus、magnus 词族，以及成对的 maximize／minimize。

normal.en: Maximum is the top of a scale and -ize means 'to make'. Maximize is simply 'to make maximum'.
normal.cn: maximum 是刻度的顶端，-ize 意为“使……”。maximize 就是“使达到最大”。

normal.en: Maximus is the Latin superlative of magnus 'great'; the same root gives magnify, magnitude and magnate.
normal.cn: maximus 是拉丁语 magnus“大”的最高级；同一词根还给出 magnify、magnitude、magnate。

normal.en: Maximize and minimize were both recorded in 1802, both in Bentham: one drives to the top of the scale, the other to the bottom.
normal.cn: maximize 与 minimize 都记录于 1802 年，都出自边沁：一个把刻度推到顶，一个推到低。

normal.en: In business writing maximize collocates with profit, efficiency, output and returns — quantities that can be read off a dial.
normal.cn: 在商业写作里，maximize 常与 profit、efficiency、output、returns 搭配——都是能从刻度盘上读出来的量。

normal.en: In computing, maximize is the button that makes a window fill the screen; the screen is the ceiling of that scale.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，maximize 是让窗口占满屏幕的那个按钮；屏幕就是那把尺子的天花板。

abstract.en: Picture a dial with a hard stop at the right end. You can turn it as far as the stop and no further; that stop is what maximum means.
abstract.cn: 想象一只右端有硬止点的旋钮。你能拧到止点，再也不能多拧一格；那个止点就是 maximum 的含义。

abstract.en: A maximum is a ceiling, not a direction: maximizing tells you where to stop, not how to get there.
abstract.cn: 最大值是天花板，不是方向：maximize 告诉你该停在哪里，却没告诉你该怎么走到那里。

abstract.en: When one quantity is maximized, others are usually spent: maximum contrast costs comfort, maximum output costs rest.
abstract.cn: 当一个量被最大化，其他量通常被花掉：最大的对比度要付出舒适，最大的产量要付出休息。

examples.en: Farmers use every hectare to maximize the harvest.
examples.cn: 农民用尽每一公顷土地，把收成做到最大。

examples.en: The software maximizes screen space by hiding the toolbar.
examples.cn: 这款软件通过隐藏工具栏把屏幕空间用到最大。

examples.en: Negotiators tried to maximize the settlement without losing the deal.
examples.cn: 谈判者试图在不丢单的情况下把和解条件做到最好。

dict_mnemonic.text: “麦克西麦子”——麦克把麦子一层层堆到仓顶，堆到再也放不下一粒 → maximize 最大化、推到顶

root: 由 maximum“最大限度”加 -ize“使……”构成，maximum 又来自拉丁语 maximus“最大的”，核心是“把某物推到刻度的最右端”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of maximize, all from one gesture: a dial is turned to the far right until it will go no further, whether the scale measures a function, a profit, an output, a chance, or a window.
sensesIntro.cn: maximize 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把旋钮一路拧到最右端，直到再也拧不动——无论这把尺子量的是函数、利润、产量、机会还是一扇窗口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial turned to the far right until it stops at the top of its scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旋钮被拧到最右端，停在刻度的顶点。

branches.en: MEASURED QUANTITIES: functions and probabilities sit on numeric scales, and maximizing moves the value to the top of that scale.
branches.cn: 可测的量：函数与概率都落在数值刻度上，最大化就是把取值推到这段刻度的顶端。

branches.en: PRODUCTION: profit and output are the business dials, and maximizing runs them at full capacity.
branches.cn: 生产：利润与产量是商业里的旋钮，最大化就是让它们满负荷运转。

branches.en: FORCE AND EXTREME: impact is a force pushed to full reach; driving one feature alone turns the word critical.
branches.cn: 力量与极端：影响是一种被推到最远的力量；只把某一特征推到顶，就让这个词带上了批评意味。

branches.en: RESOURCES: every unit is put to work, so the measure becomes the absence of idle capacity.
branches.cn: 资源：每个单位都被投入使用，于是衡量的对象变成了“没有闲置产能”。

branches.en: DEVICES AND FITNESS: a window grows to the screen's ceiling, and fitness rises to the highest value selection can reach.
branches.cn: 设备与适应度：窗口长到屏幕这层天花板，适应度升到选择所能达到的最高值。

intro.en: Maximize is built from a complete noun plus a living suffix, so its parts are easy to see: maximum + -ize. The same Latin superlative also supplies a large family of size words.
intro.cn: maximize 由一个完整名词加一个活后缀构成，部件一眼可见：maximum 加 -ize。同一个拉丁最高级还供应了一大群表示“大小”的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin maximus 'greatest' is the superlative of magnus 'great'. Both are ordinary Latin adjectives, and maximum is the neuter form used as a noun; the PIE superlative suffix *-samo- is preserved in maximus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 maximus“最大的”是 magnus“大的”的最高级。两者都是普通拉丁形容词，maximum 是作名词用的中性形式；原始印欧语最高级后缀 *-samo- 保留在 maximus 里。

items.meaning: to make as great as possible
items.meaningCN: 使尽可能大；最大化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: They maximized the grant by matching it with local funds.
items.exampleCN: 他们用地方资金配套，把拨款的作用做到最大。

items.meaningCN: 最大量；最大限度（-um 为中性最高级词尾）
items.example: The tank holds a maximum of forty litres.
items.exampleCN: 这个罐子最多装四十升。

items.meaningCN: 最大的；达到最大限度的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The drug was given at its maximal safe dose.
items.exampleCN: 这种药按最大安全剂量给予。

items.meaning: the process of making something as great as possible
items.meaningCN: 最大化；最大化过程（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Profit maximization was not the only goal of the reform.
items.exampleCN: 利润最大化并不是这场改革的唯一目标。

items.meaningCN: 追求最大化的人或物（-er 表示行为者）
items.example: As a maximizer, she never settles for the second-best option.
items.exampleCN: 作为一个凡事求最大的人，她从不接受次优选项。

items.meaning: the maximum; to reach the maximum level
items.meaningCN: 最大值；达到最高水平（maximum 的缩略）
items.example: He maxed out his credit card before the trip.
items.exampleCN: 出发前他把信用卡刷到了额度上限。

items.example: The report advises firms to maximise energy efficiency.
items.exampleCN: 报告建议企业把能效做到最大。

items.meaning: a short rule of conduct or general truth
items.meaningCN: 格言；行为准则（来自拉丁语 maxima propositio，与 maximum 同形不同源）
items.example: The maxim 'less is more' guided the whole design.
items.exampleCN: “少即是多”这句格言指导了整个设计。

items.meaningCN: 放大；使显得更大（magni- 大 + -fy 使）
items.example: The lens magnifies the print for easy reading.
items.exampleCN: 这片透镜把字放大，便于阅读。

items.meaningCN: 巨大；重要性；量级（magni- 大 + -tude 状态）
items.example: Few understood the magnitude of the loss.
items.exampleCN: 很少有人明白这次损失有多大。

items.meaning: a powerful person in business or industry
items.meaningCN: 巨头；大亨（拉丁语 magnates“大人物”）
items.example: A shipping magnate funded the new museum.
items.exampleCN: 一位航运巨头出资建了这座新博物馆。

latinEntries.structure: neuter of maximus, used as a noun
latinEntries.meaningCN: 最大者；最大量（maximus 的中性形式作名词）

definition_zh: 联合政府；多党联合内阁；联合执政的一届任期；多数联合政府；少数联合政府；大联合政府；看守联合政府；地方联合执政
definition_en: a government formed by two or more parties that agree on a shared programme and divide the cabinet posts between them
core_image: 两排原本各站一边的人把旗子并到同一张长桌后，在一份分工名单上共同落笔
scene: 大选得票分散，没有任何党派拿到过半席位，参政党派的谈判代表隔着长桌逐条核对部长职位，最后把共同纲领摊在桌面中央。 A coalition government was sworn in after no party won a majority.
sceneCN: 大选后各党得票分散，参政党派的代表隔着长桌核对部长职位，最后把共同纲领摊在桌面中央；句中的短语指「由多个政党协议共组的内阁」（第 1 个义项：两个以上政党签约共同执政、按协议分配部长席位）。图中可辨识物件：长桌、部长职位清单、共同纲领、并排的党旗、宣誓用的文件夹。

联合执政的时期；一届联合任期
作定语，指联合政府的（纲领、政策、纪律）

collocations.zh: 由最大党主导的联合政府

senses.title: Parties agree to govern as one
senses.titleCN: 两个以上政党签约共同执政
senses.definition: the cabinet that results when two or more parties sign a common programme and divide the ministerial posts between them
senses.definitionCN: 两个以上政党签署共同纲领、分配部长职位之后形成的内阁
senses.example: After weeks of bargaining, the two parties announced a coalition government.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数周讨价还价，两党宣布组成联合政府。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'grow together': separate parties, like separate shoots, fuse into one body at the negotiating table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「长到一起」：原本分开的政党像分开的枝条，在谈判桌边合成一个整体。

senses.title: The cabinet as a working body
senses.titleCN: 作为运转班子的联合内阁本身
senses.definition: the group of ministers drawn from the partner parties, considered as one body with its own meetings, papers and staff
senses.definitionCN: 由各伙伴党派抽调部长组成的班子，作为有会议、文件与班底的单一机构来看待
senses.example: The coalition government held its first cabinet meeting on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 联合内阁在周一召开了第一次内阁会议。
senses.why: Once the bargain is signed, the arrangement turns into an institution: the phrase stops naming the deal and starts naming the people who meet each week.
senses.whyCN: 协议签署之后，这个安排就变成机构：此时这个短语不再指那笔交易，而指每周开会的那批人。

senses.title: The term served under such a cabinet
senses.definition: the stretch of time from the swearing-in to the break-up during which the partners govern together
senses.definitionCN: 从宣誓就职到合作破裂之间、各党共同执政的那段时间
senses.example: That coalition government survived only fourteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 那一届联合政府只维持了十四个月。
senses.why: A cabinet is an event with a beginning and an end, so the same phrase can name the whole span rather than the body.
senses.whyCN: 一届内阁是有始有终的事件，因此同一个短语也能指整段时间，而不只是那个班子。

senses.title: A partnership with a majority
senses.titleCN: 席位过半、无需外援即可立法的联合政府
senses.definition: a partnership whose combined seats pass half the chamber, so it can legislate without help from outside parties
senses.definitionCN: 各党席位相加超过议会半数，无需外部政党支持即可立法的联合政府
senses.example: The two centre parties had enough seats for a majority coalition government.
senses.exampleCN: 两个中间派政党的席位足以组成多数联合政府。
senses.why: Seat arithmetic decides how strong the fusion is: a majority turns the partnership into a self-sufficient machine.
senses.whyCN: 席位算术决定这种合并有多结实：席位过半就把伙伴关系变成一台自足的机器。

senses.title: A partnership living on outside votes
senses.titleCN: 未过半、靠外部支持维持的少数联合政府
senses.definition: a partnership that holds office without half the seats, relying on the votes of parties outside the cabinet
senses.definitionCN: 席位不到半数、依靠内阁之外政党的投票维持执政的联合政府
senses.example: A minority coalition government must negotiate every budget with independents.
senses.exampleCN: 少数联合政府每份预算都得与独立议员协商。
senses.why: Growing together without a majority leaves the seam visible: every bill tests whether the partners can still hold hands.
senses.whyCN: 没有过半就合到一起，接缝始终露在外面：每一份法案都在检验伙伴们还能不能继续牵手。

senses.title: A grand bargain between the big rivals
senses.titleCN: 两大对手政党合组的大联合政府
senses.definition: an arrangement in which the two largest rival parties, normally opponents, share the cabinet during a crisis
senses.definitionCN: 通常在危机时期由两个最大的对立政党分享内阁的安排
senses.example: A grand coalition government was the only way out of the deadlock.
senses.exampleCN: 大联合政府是走出僵局的唯一办法。
senses.why: The fusion is most surprising when the partners were enemies: the phrase keeps its literal force, two things made one.
senses.whyCN: 当伙伴原本是敌人时，这种合并最出人意料：这个短语仍保留字面力量——两样东西变成一样。

senses.title: A stopgap cabinet
senses.titleCN: 看守或过渡性的联合政府
senses.definition: a temporary partnership that keeps the state running until a fresh election or a lasting agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在新选举或持久协议达成之前维持国家运转的临时联合班子
senses.example: A caretaker coalition government supervised the ballot and then resigned.
senses.exampleCN: 看守联合政府主持了投票，随后辞职。
senses.why: If the parties cannot yet agree on a full term, they can still agree on a short one: fusion with an expiry date.
senses.whyCN: 如果各党暂时无法就完整任期达成一致，仍可就一个短任期达成一致：带到期日的合并。

senses.title: The same device at local level
senses.titleCN: 地方与地区层面的联合执政
senses.definition: the same arrangement in a city, region or devolved assembly, often used to keep a single rival party out of office
senses.definitionCN: 在市、地区或下放权力的议会中采用的同一安排，常用来把某个对手政党挡在执政位置之外
senses.example: At city hall a coalition government of two small groups replaced the long-ruling party.
senses.exampleCN: 在市政厅，两个小党派的联合政府取代了长期执政的党。
senses.why: The pattern is scale-free: wherever seats are counted and posts are divided, partners can grow together.
senses.whyCN: 这种模式不分尺度：只要席位需要清点、职位需要分配，伙伴们就能合到一起。

intro.en: The word starts in Latin as an image of things growing into one another. Its use for a cabinet is a modern political extension rather than part of the original meaning, and coalition ministries were already called by that name in the late eighteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里最初是「事物彼此长合」的画面。用它指内阁属于近代的政治延伸，并非原义；十八世纪晚期的联合内阁已被这样称呼。

items.en: Alere 'to nourish, to feed' gave alescere, a verb meaning to begin to grow; the same family lies behind adolescent and adult.
items.cn: 意为「滋养、喂养」的拉丁动词衍生出「开始生长」的动词；「青少年」与「成年人」这两个英语词也出自同一族。

items.en: Co- 'together' plus alescere 'begin to grow' made coalescere 'to grow together, to fuse'; its past participle coalitus is the base of the noun of union.
items.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加「开始生长」，构成「长到一起、合而为一」的拉丁动词；其过去分词是「联合」这一名词的基础。

items.en: The noun coalitio, built on that participle, named a growing together or a league; English took the political sense through French coalition, where it had meant a league of powers.
items.cn: 由该分词构成的拉丁名词指「长合」或「同盟」；英语经法语借入这一政治用法，法语中它曾指列强之间的同盟。

items.en: In seventeenth and eighteenth century French, coalition meant a temporary league of states or parties formed against a common rival.
items.cn: 在十七、十八世纪的法语里，这个词指国家或党派为对付共同对手而结成的临时同盟。

items.en: British politics applied it to cabinets: the Fox-North ministry of 1783 was widely called a coalition, and the label stuck to any multi-party cabinet.
items.cn: 英国政治把它用到内阁上：一七八三年的福克斯与诺斯联合内阁被普遍称作联合政府，此后任何多党内阁都沿用这一称呼。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase widened to cover majority and minority coalitions, grand coalitions of rivals, caretaker cabinets and coalitions in devolved assemblies.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个短语扩展到涵盖多数与少数联合政府、由对手组成的大联合政府、看守内阁，以及下放权力议会中的联合执政。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to the headword, and only one of them shares its root; the second group names neighbouring arrangements that are not the same thing.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上与词条接近，其中只有一个与它同源；第二组是相邻但不等同的制度安排。

entries.definition: The noun for any union of groups; on its own it can be a campaign alliance, an electoral pact or a business bloc, with no cabinet involved.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何团体结成的联合体；单独使用时可以指竞选同盟、选举协议或商业联盟，并不涉及内阁。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun comes: separate parts merge into one mass, as cells or ideas do. It never means to form a cabinet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词所由来的动词：分开的部分合并成一团，如细胞或想法；它从不表示组阁。

entries.definition: The process of merging, used in physics and linguistics; it names the fusing, not the resulting body.
entries.definitionCN: 合并的过程，用于物理学与语言学；它指合并本身，而非合并后的机构。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb meaning 'to bring together', but it means comparing texts or gathering pages, not a political union.
entries.definitionCN: 出自意为「带到一起」的拉丁动词，但指比对文本或整理书页，与政治联合无关。

entries.definition: A general agreement to work together, often between states or parties and often for one purpose only; it need not produce a cabinet.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指合作约定，常见于国家或政党之间，往往只为一件事，不必产生内阁。

entries.definition: The name used when most parties join a cabinet to face a war, a collapse or a transition; the emphasis is on ending division, not on seat arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 多数党派为应对战争、崩溃或过渡而加入内阁时用的名称；强调结束分裂，而非席位数。

entries.definition: A cabinet formed by a single party that lacks a majority and governs with outside support; only one party holds the posts.
entries.definitionCN: 由单一政党组成、席位不过半、靠外部支持执政的内阁；部长职位只由一个党占有。

entries.definition: A chamber where no party has a majority; it is the situation that makes coalitions necessary, not the cabinet itself.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何政党过半的议会；它是促成联合政府的局面，而不是内阁本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin picture, the real word family and the real political phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语画面、真实的同族词与真实的政治说法。

normal.en: Co- 'together' plus a root meaning 'grow': two parties growing into one trunk.
normal.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加表示「生长」的词根：两个政党长成一根主干。

normal.en: The family runs coalition, coalesce, coalescence, coalitionist and coalitional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括表示联合的名词、表示合并的动词、表示合并过程的名词，以及联合派与联盟形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the trade: form a coalition government, a grand coalition government, a caretaker coalition government.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出这一行当：组成联合政府、大联合政府、看守联合政府。

normal.en: Historical anchor: the Fox-North ministry of 1783 was already called a coalition, long before the phrase became ordinary.
normal.cn: 历史锚点：一七八三年的福克斯与诺斯内阁已被称作联合政府，远早于这个短语变得平常。

normal.en: Arithmetic anchor: majority and minority coalitions differ by seats, grand coalitions by the size of the partners.
normal.cn: 算术锚点：多数与少数联合政府差在席位，大联合政府差在伙伴的体量。

abstract.en: Two chairs face away from each other until someone turns both toward one table.
abstract.cn: 两把椅子本来背对着，直到有人把它们一起转向同一张桌子。

abstract.en: A post list is circled in two colours of ink, and every name carries two signatures.
abstract.cn: 一张职位名单被两种颜色的墨水圈过，每个名字后面都有两个签名。

abstract.en: A borrowed car with two drivers: it moves, but both hands sit on the wheel.
abstract.cn: 一辆借来的车有两个司机：车能走，但方向盘上有两双手。

examples.en: The coalition government fell when the junior partner withdrew its ministers.
examples.cn: 小党撤回部长后，联合政府垮台了。

examples.en: Economists warned that a coalition government would struggle to pass a budget.
examples.cn: 经济学家警告说，联合政府将难以通过预算。

examples.en: She covered the coalition government for a regional paper.
examples.cn: 她为一家地区报纸报道这届联合政府。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「科阿利申·政府」——谐音「合力伸」：各党把力气合起来，伸到同一张桌子上办事 → 联合政府

root: 拉丁 coalescere「长到一起」= co-（共同）+ alescere「生长」，源自 alere「滋养」；名词经法语进入英语，政府义为十九世纪后的政治用法。短语后半出自拉丁 gubernare「掌舵」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bargain: parties grow together, sign a programme, meet as a body, hold office for a term, and then vary by seats, by the size of the partners, by how long the deal lasts and by the level of government.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一笔交易展开：各党长到一起、签下纲领、作为班子开会、执政一个任期，随后再按席位多寡、伙伴体量、协议时长与政府层级分化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate parties grow into one cabinet, then hold office until the seam shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：分开的政党长成一个内阁，然后执政到接缝暴露。

branches.en: THE DEAL AND ITS WEAK FORM: a signed fusion, and the version that survives without half the seats.
branches.cn: 协议与弱势版本：签约合并，以及席位不到半数仍能存活的那种。

branches.en: BODY AND BIG TWO: a weekly cabinet meeting, and the crisis version built from the largest rivals.
branches.cn: 班子与两大党：每周开会的内阁，以及由最大对手在危机中搭成的那种。

branches.en: FULL TERM AND STOPGAP: a term that runs its course, and a term with an expiry date set by the next election.
branches.cn: 完整任期与过渡任期：走完全程的任期，以及把到期日定在下一次选举的任期。

branches.en: MAJORITY: seats beyond half make the partnership self-sufficient.
branches.cn: 多数：席位过半使伙伴关系自足。

branches.en: LOCAL: the same device in a council or devolved assembly, scaled down but identical in logic.
branches.cn: 地方层面：同一装置用于市议会或下放议会，规模缩小而逻辑相同。

intro.en: The phrase is a noun plus a noun, and both halves are built from Latin pieces that also form many other English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词合成，而两半都由拉丁语构件搭起，这些构件还构成许多别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Coalescere supplies the first noun through its participle; gubernare supplies the second through French; the suffixes -ition and -ment turn actions into nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词「长到一起」经其分词提供第一个名词；拉丁动词「掌舵」经法语提供第二个名词的动词；表示动作的名词后缀把动作变成名词。

items.example: The prefix binds two separate things into one act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分开的两样东西绑进同一个动作。

items.structure: co- + alescere (Latin root, 'to begin to grow')
items.meaningCN: 表示「生长、开始生长」的词根
items.example: The root pictures a shoot putting out new wood.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根画出新枝抽出新木的画面。

items.meaningCN: 表示「动作或其结果」的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix turns the act of fusing into a countable noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「合并」这一动作变成可数名词。

items.meaning: a union of parties or groups
items.meaningCN: 党派或团体结成的联合体
items.example: The coalition held together for a full term.
items.exampleCN: 这个联合体撑满了整个任期。

items.meaning: the body that runs a state
items.example: The government published its spending plans.

items.structure: govern (verb base, from Latin gubernare 'to steer')
items.exampleCN: 联合政府靠妥协来治理。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示「动作的结果或手段」的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix makes the act of steering into an institution.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「掌舵」的动作变成一种机构。

items.meaningCN: 主张多党联合执政的人
items.example: The coalitionist defended the deal to both party boards.
items.exampleCN: 这位联合派向两个党的执委会为这笔协议辩护。

items.example: Coalitional discipline held through the budget vote.
items.exampleCN: 联合体的纪律在预算表决中维持住了。

items.example: The governmental reshuffle followed the election.
items.exampleCN: 选举之后发生了政府改组。

items.example: An intergovernmental panel reviewed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 一个政府间小组审查了该计划。

definition_en: Relating to bacteriology, the study of bacteria; of methods or weapons that use bacteria.
core_image: 培养皿、显微镜与检验单构成的那一整套学问
scene: 实验室做过细菌学检测，确认水源没有污染。 The lab ran bacteriological tests and cleared the water supply.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bacteriological 指与细菌学这门研究有关的。

pos.zh: 细菌学的；以细菌为手段的

forms.label: 形容词原级（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Of the science of bacteria
senses.definition: belonging to bacteriology, the branch of biology that studies bacteria
senses.definitionCN: 属于细菌学，即研究细菌的生物学分支
senses.example: She published a bacteriological survey of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 她发表了一份关于那条河的细菌学调查。
senses.why: The word stacks bacterio-, small rod, with -logy, study, and -ical, relating to, so it means of the study of bacteria.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 bacterio-「小棍」、-logy「学问」与 -ical「与……有关的」叠在一起，因此意为「与细菌研究有关的」。

senses.title: Using bacteria as a means
senses.definition: of tests, weapons or processes that work by means of bacteria rather than by studying them
senses.definitionCN: 指依靠细菌本身而非研究细菌来发挥作用的检测、武器或工艺
senses.example: The treaty bans bacteriological weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约禁止细菌武器。
senses.why: Because the science handles the organisms, its adjective came to label anything that puts them to work.
senses.whyCN: 因为这门科学处理这些微生物，它的形容词便用来标记任何把它们投入使用的事物。

intro.en: Bacteriological is bacteriology plus -ical; bacteriology joins Greek bakterion, a small staff, with -logia, study, and was coined in the 1880s.
intro.cn: bacteriological 是 bacteriology 加 -ical；bacteriology 由希腊语 bakterion「小棍」与 -logia「学问」组成，于 1880 年代造出。

items.en: Greek bakterion meant a small staff, a diminutive of bakteria, a walking stick.
items.cn: 希腊语 bakterion 意为「小棍」，是 bakteria「手杖」的指小形式。

items.en: Naturalists took the word as bacterium for rod-shaped microbes seen under the lens.
items.cn: 博物学者借该词作 bacterium，指镜下所见的杆状微生物。

items.en: Greek -logia meant an account or study, from logos, word or reason.
items.cn: 希腊语 -logia 意为「论述、学问」，出自 logos「言辞、理性」。

items.en: Bacteriology was coined in the 1880s as the new discipline took shape.
items.cn: 随着这门新学科成形，bacteriology 于 1880 年代造出。

items.en: The adjective followed within a decade, used of tests and laboratories.
items.cn: 形容词在十年内随之出现，用于检测与实验室。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word gained the sense of using bacteria as weapons.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词获得「以细菌为武器」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the bacterium family; the near-meaning group lists other adjectives of the life sciences.
note.cn: 形近组保留 bacterium 词族；近义组列出生命科学的其他形容词。

normalIntro.cn: bacteriological 是 bacterio 加 logy 加 ical：与研究那些「小棍」有关的。

normal.en: Bacterial is of bacteria; bacteriological is of the science.
normal.cn: bacterial 指细菌本身，bacteriological 指这门科学。

normal.en: The noun is bacteriology, the person bacteriologist.
normal.cn: 名词是 bacteriology，人是 bacteriologist。

normal.en: Tests and analysis are the commonest nouns after it.
normal.cn: 其后最常见的名词是 tests 与 analysis。

normal.en: Bacteriological warfare is a set term.
normal.cn: bacteriological warfare 是固定术语。

normal.en: The shorter bacteriologic also exists.
normal.cn: 较短的 bacteriologic 也存在。

abstract.en: Picture a rack of dishes under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯下一排培养皿。

abstract.en: Imagine a report clearing a village well.
abstract.cn: 想象一份为村中水井开绿灯的报告。

abstract.en: Think of a science turned into a weapon.
abstract.cn: 想象一门科学被变成武器。

examples.en: Bacteriological tests confirmed the source.
examples.cn: 细菌学检测确认了来源。

examples.en: The hospital opened a bacteriological unit.
examples.cn: 医院开设了一个细菌学部门。

examples.en: Bacteriological contamination closed the beach.
examples.cn: 细菌污染使海滩关闭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：bacterio「小棍、细菌」+ logy「学问」+ -ical「……的」——与细菌这门学问有关的，就是 bacteriological。

root: 希腊语 bakterion「小棍」被借作 bacterium「细菌」，加 -logia「学问」于 1880 年代成 bacteriology；再加 -ical 成 bacteriological。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses belong to the same discipline: describing the study of bacteria, and describing what puts bacteria to use.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项同属一门学科：描述对细菌的研究，以及描述把细菌投入使用的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dishes, a microscope and a test report as one body of learning
core.cn: 核心意象：培养皿、显微镜与检验单构成的那一整套学问

branches.en: Tests clearing a water supply.
branches.cn: 为供水开绿灯的检测。

branches.cn: 发表的河流调查报告。

branches.en: Weapons banned by treaty.
branches.cn: 被条约禁止的武器。

branches.en: Contamination closing a beach.

branches.en: One science, studied or applied.
branches.cn: 同一门科学，或被研究或被应用。

intro.en: Bacteriological is bacterio plus logy plus ical; the same -logy builds biology and pathology, and -ist names the specialist.
intro.cn: bacteriological 是 bacterio 加 logy 加 ical；同一 -logy 构成 biology 与 pathology，而 -ist 指专家。

latinIntro.en: The layers are Greek: bakterion, a small staff, logos, account, and bios, life; Latin sterilis gives sterile beside them.
latinIntro.cn: 各层均属希腊语：bakterion「小棍」、logos「论述」与 bios「生命」；旁边的拉丁语 sterilis 产生 sterile。

definition_zh: adj. 恰当的，贴切的；易于……的，有……倾向的；（学生）聪慧的，一学就会的
definition_en: Exactly suited to the purpose or occasion; inclined or liable to do something; of a learner, quick to pick things up.
core_image: 正好合得上那个槽口，一放就到位
scene: 这个比喻用得恰到好处。 It was an apt metaphor for a fragile economy.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apt 指某句话或某个说法正好贴合眼下的情形，不多不少。

senses.title: Exactly suited
senses.definition: so well fitted to the situation that it seems made for it, used of words, names and comparisons
senses.definitionCN: 与情形贴合得仿佛专为它而造，用于词语、名称与比喻
senses.example: Silence was the aptest reply he could give.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默是他能给出的最贴切的回答。
senses.why: The Latin source means fastened or fitted, so an apt phrase is one that clicks into the situation like a part into its slot.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「装好的、合上的」，所以 apt 的说法就像零件卡进槽口一样合上眼下的情形。

senses.title: Inclined or liable
senses.definition: having a tendency to do something, in the pattern apt to plus a verb
senses.definitionCN: 有做某事的倾向，用于 apt to 加动词的句式
senses.example: Old pipes are apt to burst in a hard frost.
senses.exampleCN: 旧水管在严寒中容易爆裂。
senses.why: If a thing fits a slot, it slides there easily, so fitted turns into likely: the behaviour is the groove it naturally runs in.
senses.whyCN: 东西合得上槽口就容易滑进去，于是「合上」引申为「易于」：那种行为就是它天然会走的沟槽。

senses.title: Quick to learn
senses.definition: of a person, especially a pupil, ready and able to take in new skills
senses.definitionCN: 指人尤其是学生，能迅速接受新技能
senses.example: She was an apt student of the violin.
senses.exampleCN: 她学小提琴一点就通。
senses.why: Here the fit is between the learner and the subject: the mind takes the shape of what it is taught without resistance.
senses.whyCN: 这里合得上的是学习者与所学：头脑毫无阻力地长成所教内容的形状。

intro.en: Apt is Latin aptus, fitted, the past participle of apere, to fasten. The same root gives adapt, adept, inept and aptitude.
intro.cn: apt 就是拉丁语 aptus「合好的」，是 apere「系紧、装上」的过去分词。同一词根产生 adapt、adept、inept 与 aptitude。

items.en: Latin apere meant to fasten or attach one thing to another, a verb of joining rather than of choosing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 apere 意为「把一物系到另一物上」，是表「连接」而非「挑选」的动词。

items.en: The participle aptus meant fastened, hence fitted and suitable: the part is already in its place.
items.cn: 过去分词 aptus 意为「系好的」，进而指「合适的」：零件已经就位。

items.en: Greek haptein, to fasten, is a cousin of apere, which shows the root is older than Latin itself.
items.cn: 希腊语 haptein「系紧」与 apere 同源，说明这个词根比拉丁语本身更古老。

items.en: English borrowed apt in the late fourteenth century for something suited to its purpose.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪末借入 apt，表示某物与其用途相合。

items.en: Around the 1590s apt gained the sense of prone or liable, and also the sense of a quick learner.
items.cn: 1590 年代前后，apt 增加了「易于、往往」之义，也增加了「学得快」之义。

items.en: The same root builds adapt, to fit to, adept, thoroughly fitted, and inept, not fitted at all.
items.cn: 同一词根构成 adapt「使合上」、adept「完全合上、熟练」与 inept「完全合不上、笨拙」。

note.en: The look-alike group is a family lesson: adept is skilled, inept is clumsy, adapt is to make fit; the near-meaning group gives the plain synonyms.
note.cn: 形近组是一堂家族课：adept 是熟练，inept 是笨拙，adapt 是使合适；近义组给出朴素同义词。

normalIntro.en: Apt means fitted: a phrase that fits the moment, a habit that fits the person, a mind that fits the subject.

normal.en: Apt is short and formal; suitable is the safe everyday word.
normal.cn: apt 简短而正式，suitable 是稳妥的日常词。

abstract.en: Picture a key sliding into its own lock.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙滑进属于它的那把锁。

abstract.en: Imagine a nickname that fits like a glove.
abstract.cn: 想象一个贴得像手套的外号。

abstract.en: Think of a groove a ball keeps rolling back into.
abstract.cn: 想象一条球总会滚回去的沟槽。

examples.en: The title is apt: the book really is about waiting.
examples.cn: 书名很贴切：这本书写的确实就是等待。

examples.en: He is apt to promise more than he can deliver.
examples.cn: 他往往承诺得比能做到的多。

examples.en: An apt pupil needs showing only once.
examples.cn: 一学就会的学生只需示范一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：apt 与 adapt 同根，本义「合得上」——话合得上场面就是贴切，人合得上学问就是聪慧。

root: 拉丁语 apere「系紧、装上」的过去分词 aptus「合好的」，经法语进入英语作 apt；由「合上槽口」引申出「贴切」「易于」与「学得快」三义。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses are one fit: words fitting a moment, a person fitting a habit, and a mind fitting a subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项是同一种「合上」：词语合上此刻，人合上某种习惯，头脑合上一门学问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a part dropping straight into its own slot
core.cn: 核心意象：正好合得上那个槽口，一放就到位

branches.en: A nickname that fits perfectly.

branches.en: Silence as the best reply.

branches.en: Old pipes bursting in a frost.

branches.en: A pupil who needs one demonstration.
branches.cn: 只需示范一遍的学生。

branches.en: Both slide easily into a groove.
branches.cn: 两者都轻易滑进沟槽。

intro.en: Apt is the fit root itself, and with ad-, in- and -itude it builds adapt, inept and aptitude.
intro.cn: apt 本身就是「合」词根，加上 ad-、in- 与 -itude 便构成 adapt、inept 与 aptitude。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is apere, to fasten, and its participle aptus, fitted; Greek haptein is the older cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 apere「系紧」及其分词 aptus「合好的」；希腊语 haptein 是更古老的同源词。

definition_zh: adj. 人为的；由人类活动造成的（尤指环境变化）
definition_en: Caused by human activity rather than by natural processes, especially of pollution, warming or landscape change.
core_image: 变化曲线在人类出现那一格突然抬头
scene: 报告把升温主要归因于人类排放。 Anthropogenic emissions drive most of the warming.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：报告区分自然因素与人类活动，anthropogenic 专指后者，即由人类排放造成的那部分升温。

pos.zh: 人为的；人类活动造成的

forms.label: 无 -er/-est 形式（多音节形容词，用 more/most）

senses.title: Caused by human activity
senses.definition: resulting from what people do rather than from natural processes, especially of emissions and warming
senses.definitionCN: 源自人的行为而非自然过程，尤指排放与升温
senses.example: The report separates natural from anthropogenic forcing.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把自然驱动与人为驱动分开。
senses.why: Greek anthropos means human and -genes means born of, so the word literally says born of humans, which is exactly the claim being made.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anthropos 意为「人」，-genes 意为「由……而生」，所以这个词字面上说的就是「由人而生」，正是它要表达的判断。

senses.title: In wider earth science
senses.titleCN: 更广泛的地球科学用法
senses.definition: describing soils, landforms or deposits produced by human work rather than by nature
senses.definitionCN: 描述由人类劳作而非自然形成的土壤、地貌或沉积物
senses.example: The valley floor is an anthropogenic soil built by centuries of terracing.
senses.exampleCN: 谷底土壤是数百年梯田耕作形成的人为土。
senses.why: The same born-of-humans test is applied to physical features: if people made the layer, the layer is anthropogenic.
senses.whyCN: 同一条「由人而生」的判据也用于自然地貌：如果那一层是人造出来的，它就是人为的。

intro.en: Anthropogenic joins Greek anthropos, human, to -genes, born of, plus -ic. It was built in nineteenth-century science and became central to climate writing in the late twentieth.
intro.cn: anthropogenic 把希腊语 anthropos「人」与 -genes「由……而生」及 -ic 拼合。它造于 19 世纪的科学语境，20 世纪后期成为气候写作的核心词。

items.en: Greek anthropos meant a human being, and gives anthropology, anthropoid and misanthrope.
items.cn: 希腊语 anthropos 意为「人」，产生 anthropology、anthropoid 与 misanthrope。

items.en: Greek -genes meant born of or produced by, from the root gen-, to beget. It builds hydrogen, oxygen and carcinogenic.
items.cn: 希腊语 -genes 意为「由……而生、由……产生」，出自 gen-「生育」词根。它构成 hydrogen、oxygen 与 carcinogenic。

items.en: Nineteenth-century science joined the two pieces for origins caused by people, first in geology and physical anthropology.
items.cn: 19 世纪的科学把两个部件拼合，指由人造成的起源，最早用于地质学与体质人类学。

items.en: English added -ic to make the adjective, and the adverb anthropogenically followed for describing how a change was caused.
items.cn: 英语加 -ic 构成形容词，随后又出现副词 anthropogenically，用于描述变化是如何造成的。

items.en: Since the late twentieth century the word is standard in climate science, and Anthropocene names the proposed epoch of human dominance.
items.cn: 自 20 世纪后期起该词成为气候科学的标准用词，Anthropocene 则命名了以人类主导为特征的拟议地质世。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the anthropos family and the -genic ending; the near-meaning group lists other words for made by people.
note.cn: 形近组保留 anthropos 词族与 -genic 词尾；近义组列出其他表示「由人造成」的词。

normalIntro.en: Anthropogenic is anthropos plus -genic: born of humans, so caused by us rather than by nature.

normal.en: The fixed phrase is anthropogenic climate change.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 anthropogenic climate change。

normal.en: It contrasts with natural, not with artificial objects.
normal.cn: 它与 natural 相对，而不是与「人造物品」相对。

normal.en: The adverb is anthropogenically, as in anthropogenically warmed.
normal.cn: 副词是 anthropogenically，如 anthropogenically warmed。

normal.en: Carcinogenic shares -genic, so both mean produced by something.
normal.cn: carcinogenic 共用 -genic，所以两者都表示「由某物产生」。

normal.en: Do not confuse anthropogenic with anthropological, about the study of people.
normal.cn: 别把 anthropogenic 与 anthropological「关于人类研究的」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a curve that jumps upward where people appear.
abstract.cn: 想象一条在人类出现处陡然上抬的曲线。

abstract.en: Imagine a soil layer made of centuries of terracing.
abstract.cn: 想象一层由数百年梯田耕作堆成的土壤。

abstract.en: Think of a fingerprint on a climate record.
abstract.cn: 想象气候记录上留下的一枚人类指纹。

examples.en: Most of the observed warming is anthropogenic.
examples.cn: 观测到的升温大部分是人为造成的。

examples.en: The lake suffers from anthropogenic nutrient loading.
examples.cn: 这座湖泊受到人为营养盐输入的困扰。

examples.en: Anthropogenic soils cover the old terraced slopes.
examples.cn: 人为土覆盖了旧日的梯田坡面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：anthropo「人」+ genic「产生的」——由人产生的，就是人为的；气候报告里专指人类排放那一块。

root: 希腊语 anthropos「人」+ -genes「由……而生」加 -ic 构成 anthropogenic，字面即「由人而生的」，用于区分自然成因与人类活动成因。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses apply one test: was this born of humans? The answer labels emissions and warming, and also soils and landforms.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在用同一条判据：这是由人而生的吗？答案既标注排放与升温，也标注土壤与地貌。

intro.en: Anthropogenic is anthropos plus -gen plus -ic, and each piece builds a large scientific family.
intro.cn: anthropogenic 是 anthropos 加 -gen 加 -ic，每个部件都能撑起一个庞大的科学词族。

latinIntro.en: Both pieces are Greek: anthropos, human, and -genes, born of. Latin only supplied the -ic ending through French.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部件都是希腊语：anthropos「人」与 -genes「由……而生」。拉丁语只经法语提供了 -ic 词尾。
