definition_zh: n. 应用程序；手机应用（application 的截短形式）
definition_en: A software application, especially one downloaded to a phone or tablet; the everyday short form of application, now a normal word in its own right.
core_image: 手机屏幕上那一格格点开就用的小图标
scene: 这款应用把整本词典装进了口袋。 The app puts the whole dictionary in your pocket.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：app 是 application 的截短，指手机或电脑上的一个应用程序。

senses.title: A software application
senses.definition: a program designed to do a particular job for the user, on any computer or device
senses.definitionCN: 为用户完成某项具体任务的程序，可在任何电脑或设备上运行
senses.example: The desktop app syncs your notes across machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个桌面应用能在多台设备间同步笔记。
senses.why: App is simply the first syllable of application kept as a whole word, so it covers any application, not only phone ones.
senses.whyCN: app 就是把 application 的第一个音节留下来当整词用，因此它涵盖任何应用程序，不只是手机上的。

senses.title: A phone program you download
senses.definition: in ordinary speech, one of the small icons on a phone screen that you install from a store
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中，指手机屏幕上从应用商店装来的那些小图标之一
senses.example: She deleted three apps to free up space.
senses.exampleCN: 她删了三个应用来腾出空间。
senses.why: After 2008 the store model made this the default meaning, so app now suggests a phone first and a desktop second.
senses.whyCN: 2008 年之后应用商店模式让这层意思成了默认义，如今 app 先让人想到手机，其次才是电脑。

intro.en: App is a clipping of application, which goes back to Latin applicare, to fold towards, from ad- plus plicare, to fold. The short form took off with phone stores.
intro.cn: app 是 application 的截短，而 application 可追到拉丁语 applicare「折向、贴附」，由 ad- 加 plicare「折」构成。这个短形式随手机应用商店流行开来。

items.en: Latin plicare meant to fold. It gives English apply, imply, complicate, reply and explicit.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为「折叠」。它产生英语的 apply、imply、complicate、reply 与 explicit。

items.en: Adding ad-, to, gave applicare, to fold towards or join to, hence to put one thing onto another.
items.cn: 加上 ad-「向」得到 applicare「折向、贴附」，因此引申为把一物放到另一物上。

items.en: The noun applicatio meant a joining to, and in later Latin the act of putting something to use.
items.cn: 名词 applicatio 意为「贴附」，在后期拉丁语中指「投入使用」这一动作。

items.en: English took application in the fifteenth century for putting a thing to a purpose, and later for a formal request.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪吸收 application，表示「把某物用于某目的」，后来又指正式申请。

items.en: From the 1960s application named a program written for a user's task, as opposed to system software.
items.cn: 自 1960 年代起，application 指为用户任务编写的程序，与系统软件相对。

items.en: Programmers shortened application to app in the 1980s, and the 2008 phone stores made it an everyday word.
items.cn: 1980 年代程序员把 application 缩为 app，2008 年的手机应用商店让它成为日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against apt and ape, which differ by one letter; the near-meaning group gives the fuller words for the same thing.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只差一个字母的 apt、ape 混淆；近义组给出指同一事物的更完整说法。

entries.definition: Suitable or quick to learn.
A tailless primate; to copy.
A high mountain peak.
A round fruit; also a tech brand.
entries.definitionCN: 一种圆形水果；也指一个科技品牌。

entries.definition: The unshortened word for app.
A set of instructions a computer runs.
entries.definitionCN: 计算机执行的一组指令。

entries.definition: Programs considered as a whole.
A small utility that does one job.

normalIntro.en: App is application cut down to its first three letters, the part you say anyway when speaking fast.
normalIntro.cn: app 就是 application 砍到只剩前三个字母，也就是你说快时本来只会念出的那一截。

normal.en: It is countable: one app, two apps.
normal.cn: 它可数：one app、two apps。

normal.en: Write app in lower case unless it starts a sentence.
normal.cn: 除句首外，app 一律小写。

normal.en: The full form application is still used in formal writing.
normal.cn: 正式书面语仍用完整形式 application。

normal.en: Do not confuse app with apt, which means suitable.
normal.cn: 别把 app 与 apt「恰当的」混淆。

normal.en: App store, app icon and app developer are fixed pairs.
normal.cn: app store、app icon、app developer 都是固定搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a grid of icons waiting for a tap.
abstract.cn: 想象一屏等着被点开的图标。

abstract.en: Imagine a long word trimmed to its first syllable.
abstract.cn: 想象一个长词被剪到只剩第一个音节。

abstract.en: Think of a whole dictionary folded into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象整本词典被折进口袋。

examples.en: The app works offline once the words are downloaded.
examples.cn: 单词下载好之后，这个应用可以离线使用。

examples.en: He builds apps for small museums.
examples.cn: 他为小型博物馆开发应用。

examples.en: Delete the apps you have not opened in a month.
examples.cn: 把一个月没打开过的应用删掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：application 掐掉后半截，只留前三个字母 app——手机上一格图标就是一个 app。

root: 拉丁语 plicare「折」加 ad-「向」成 applicare「贴附」，名词 applicatio 经法语进入英语作 application「运用、申请」；计算机时代指应用程序，1980 年代截短为 app。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one clipped word: any application on any device, and the phone application that the word now suggests first.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个截短词：任何设备上的任何应用程序，以及如今这个词最先让人想到的手机应用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the little grid of icons you tap open on a screen
core.cn: 核心意象：手机屏幕上那一格格点开就用的小图标

branches.en: A desktop program that syncs notes.
branches.cn: 同步笔记的桌面程序。

branches.en: A tool that converts one file to another.
branches.cn: 把一种文件转成另一种的工具。

branches.en: An icon installed from a store.
branches.cn: 从商店装来的一个图标。

branches.en: Three apps deleted to free space.
branches.cn: 为腾空间删掉的三个应用。

branches.en: Both are application cut short.
branches.cn: 两者都是 application 的截短。

intro.en: App hides the prefix ap- and the fold root plic-, which build apply, application, applicant, appliance and applicable.
intro.cn: app 里藏着前缀 ap- 与「折」词根 plic-，它们构成 apply、application、applicant、appliance 与 applicable。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is plicare, to fold, applicare, to fold towards, and the noun applicatio, a joining to.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 plicare「折」、applicare「折向」，以及名词 applicatio「贴附」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: plicare 是 apply 的来源。

definition_zh: n. 按蚊；疟蚊（传播疟疾的蚊属）
definition_en: A mosquito of the genus Anopheles, the only group that transmits human malaria, resting with its body tilted upward.
core_image: 停在浅水边、身子翘起来的那只细腿蚊子
scene: 村里排干了那片水洼，蚊子少了一大半。 An anopheles was found in the drained puddle.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：在那片浅水洼里发现的蚊子属于按蚊属，也就是能传播疟疾的那一类，学名 Anopheles。

senses.title: The mosquito genus
senses.definition: a mosquito of the genus Anopheles, recognisable by its raised resting posture and spotted wings
senses.definitionCN: 按蚊属的蚊子，以停息时身体上翘的姿态与带斑的翅为特征
senses.example: The anopheles rests with its abdomen pointing up.
senses.exampleCN: 按蚊停息时腹部朝上翘起。
senses.why: Greek anopheles meant useless or harmful, from an-, not, and ophelos, benefit; the name was a judgement on the insect, not a description.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anopheles 意为「无用的、有害的」，由 an-「不」与 ophelos「益处」构成；这个名字是对该昆虫的评价，而不是描述。

senses.title: The malaria vector
senses.definition: the insect considered as the carrier of malaria, the sense used in public health work
senses.definitionCN: 作为疟疾携带者的这种昆虫，是公共卫生工作中使用的义项
senses.example: Anopheles control cut the local malaria rate sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 按蚊防治使当地疟疾发病率大幅下降。
senses.why: Only this genus transmits human malaria, so in health writing the name stands for the transmission route itself.
senses.whyCN: 只有这一属传播人类疟疾，因此在卫生文献中这个名字就代表传播途径本身。

intro.en: Anopheles is Greek anopheles, useless or harmful, from an-, not, and ophelos, benefit. Meigen fixed it as the genus name in 1818.
intro.cn: anopheles 来自希腊语 anopheles「无用的、有害的」，由 an-「不」与 ophelos「益处」构成。迈根 1818 年把它定为属名。

items.en: Greek an- means not or without before a vowel, the same prefix found in anaerobic and anarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 在元音前意为「不、没有」，与 anaerobic、anarchy 中的前缀相同。

items.en: Greek ophelos meant benefit, advantage or help, and is related to ophellein, to increase or aid.
items.cn: 希腊语 ophelos 意为「益处、好处、帮助」，与 ophellein「增加、帮助」相关。

items.en: Anopheles therefore meant bringing no benefit, useless, and by extension harmful. It was an evaluative word before it was a name.
items.cn: 因此 anopheles 意为「带不来好处、无用」，引申为「有害」。它先是一个评价词，后来才成为名称。

items.en: Johann Meigen established Anopheles as the genus name in 1818, and the spelling was kept unchanged in English.
items.cn: 迈根 1818 年确立 Anopheles 为属名，英语沿用原拼写未作改动。

items.en: After Ross proved mosquito transmission of malaria in 1897, the name became central to public health, and anopheline is the adjective.
items.cn: 罗斯 1897 年证实疟疾经蚊传播后，这个名字成为公共卫生的核心词，形容词是 anopheline。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction; the near-meaning group lists other biting insects and the vector role.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 anaphylaxis「过敏性休克」混淆；近义组列出其他叮人昆虫与媒介这一角色。

entries.definition: Relating to the anopheles group.
A severe whole-body allergic reaction.
A small plant-sucking insect.
entries.definitionCN: 一种吸食植物汁液的小虫。

entries.definition: Something that departs from the norm.
Any two-winged biting fly of this family.
entries.definitionCN: 该科中任何双翅叮人蝇类。

entries.definition: An organism that carries a pathogen.
A small two-winged flying insect.
A tiny fly, some kinds of which bite.
entries.definitionCN: 一种极小的蝇，部分种类叮人。

normalIntro.en: Anopheles is an- plus ophelos: no benefit, a name that judges the insect rather than describes it.
normalIntro.cn: anopheles 就是 an- 加 ophelos：没有益处，这个名字是在评价这种昆虫，而不是描述它。

normal.en: The word is the same singular and plural: one anopheles, many anopheles.
normal.cn: 单复数同形：one anopheles、many anopheles。

normal.en: The adjective is anopheline, as in anopheline mosquito.
normal.cn: 形容词是 anopheline，如 anopheline mosquito。

normal.en: Only anopheles transmits human malaria, not ordinary house mosquitoes.
normal.cn: 只有按蚊传播人类疟疾，普通家蚊不传播。

normal.en: It rests with the body tilted up, unlike other mosquitoes.
normal.cn: 它停息时身体上翘，与其他蚊子不同。

normal.en: Do not confuse anopheles with anaphylaxis, an allergic reaction.
normal.cn: 别把 anopheles 与 anaphylaxis「过敏反应」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a thin mosquito leaning back on a leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一只细瘦的蚊子在叶子上向后倾着身子。

abstract.en: Imagine a shallow puddle full of wriggling larvae.
abstract.cn: 想象一片浅水洼里满是扭动的幼虫。

abstract.en: Think of a name that means no benefit at all.
abstract.cn: 想象一个意为「毫无益处」的名字。

examples.en: Anopheles larvae lie flat on the water surface.
examples.cn: 按蚊幼虫平躺在水面上。

examples.en: The survey mapped every anopheles breeding site.
examples.cn: 调查标出了每一处按蚊繁殖地。

examples.en: An anopheles bite can transmit the malaria parasite.
examples.cn: 按蚊叮咬可传播疟原虫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「无」+ ophel「益处」+ es——对人毫无益处的蚊子，就是按蚊、疟蚊，记住它停着时身子翘起来。

root: 希腊语 an-「无」+ ophelos「益处」构成 anopheles「无用的、有害的」，迈根 1818 年取为蚊属名 Anopheles，因该属传播疟疾而成为公共卫生关键词。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one insect: the genus with its raised posture, and the same insect seen as the route by which malaria travels.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种昆虫：身体上翘的那个蚊属，以及被视为疟疾传播途径的同一种昆虫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin mosquito tilted up beside shallow water
core.cn: 核心意象：浅水边一只翘起身子的细瘦蚊子

branches.en: A mosquito leaning back on a leaf.
branches.cn: 一只在叶子上后倾的蚊子。

branches.en: Larvae lying flat on a puddle.
branches.cn: 平躺在浅水洼上的幼虫。

branches.en: A map of breeding sites to drain.
branches.cn: 一张标出待排干繁殖地的地图。

branches.en: A bite that carries the parasite.
branches.cn: 一次携带病原虫的叮咬。

branches.en: One insect, named then feared.
branches.cn: 同一种昆虫，先被命名，后被畏惧。

intro.en: Anopheles is an- plus ophelos plus -es, and the surrounding vocabulary brings in mal-, aer- and vect-.
intro.cn: anopheles 是 an- 加 ophelos 加 -es，周边词汇还带来 mal-、aer- 与 vect-。

latinIntro.en: The name is wholly Greek: an- and ophelos. It was Latinised only in spelling when Meigen fixed the genus in 1818.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名字完全是希腊语：an- 与 ophelos。迈根 1818 年确立属名时只在拼写上作了拉丁化。

definition_zh: n. 航空；航空业；飞行活动；航空器的制造与使用
definition_en: The design, building and use of aircraft, or the activity of flying them.
core_image: 一整套让人离开地面的行当
scene: 她转行进入航空业，先做地面调度。 She moved into aviation, starting with ground dispatch.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aviation 指航空器的设计、制造与使用这一整个领域。

senses.title: The whole field of flight
senses.definition: the design, manufacture and operation of aircraft taken as one field of work
senses.definitionCN: 把航空器的设计、制造与运营视为一个工作领域
senses.example: Aviation employs millions worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 航空业在全球雇用上千万人。
senses.why: Aviation was coined from Latin avis, bird, so it names the human craft of doing what birds do.
senses.whyCN: aviation 由拉丁语 avis「鸟」造出，因此它指人类做鸟所做之事的那门技艺。

senses.title: The activity of flying
senses.definition: the practical activity of flying aircraft, sorted by who flies and for what purpose
senses.definitionCN: 驾驶航空器飞行的实际活动，按谁飞、为何飞来划分
senses.example: General aviation covers private flying.
senses.exampleCN: 通用航空涵盖私人飞行。
senses.why: Once the industry sense was fixed, the same word narrowed to the flying itself, split into civil and military branches.
senses.whyCN: 产业义固定之后，同一个词又收窄到飞行本身，分为民用与军用两支。

intro.en: Aviation is a modern coinage from Latin avis, bird, with the ending -ation; it was formed in French in the 1860s for the idea of mechanical flight.
intro.cn: aviation 是近代由拉丁语 avis「鸟」加 -ation 词尾造出的词；1860 年代在法语中成形，用来指机械飞行这一构想。

items.en: A root meaning bird lies behind aviary and the Latin word avis.
items.cn: 一个表示「鸟」的词根支撑着 aviary 与拉丁语 avis。

items.en: Latin avis meant bird, the natural model for any thought of human flight.
items.cn: 拉丁语 avis 意为「鸟」，是人类飞行构想的天然范本。

items.en: Aviarium named a place where birds were kept, giving English aviary.
items.cn: aviarium 指养鸟之处，产生英语 aviary。

items.en: A French writer coined aviation in 1863 from avis plus -ation for aerial navigation.
items.cn: 一位法国作者于 1863 年由 avis 加 -ation 造出 aviation，指空中航行。

items.en: English took the word within three years, while powered flight was still decades away.
items.cn: 英语在三年内就借入该词，而动力飞行还要等上几十年。

items.en: After 1903 the word grew into the name of a whole industry and its regulation.
items.cn: 1903 年之后，这个词扩展为整个产业及其监管的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the avi family; the near-meaning group lists other names for flight as a science or a trade.
note.cn: 形近组保留 avi 词族；近义组列出把飞行当作科学或行业的其他名称。

entries.definition: A person who flies aircraft.
A large enclosure for birds.
Aircraft electronic systems.
Very eager for something.
The science of flight.
The act of moving through the air.
Movement of goods or people by air.
Flight including space beyond air.
entries.definitionCN: 含大气层外空间的飞行领域。

normalIntro.en: Aviation is avis, bird, plus -ation: the human craft of doing what birds do.
normalIntro.cn: aviation 是 avis「鸟」加 -ation：人类做鸟所做之事的那门技艺。

normal.en: Civil aviation is the non-military side.
normal.cn: civil aviation 指非军事的一面。

normal.en: General aviation means private flying.
normal.cn: general aviation 指私人飞行。

normal.en: The word is uncountable.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数。

normal.en: Aviator is the person, aviation is the field.
normal.cn: aviator 是人，aviation 是领域。

normal.en: Aviary shares avis but keeps birds, not planes.
normal.cn: aviary 同出 avis，但装的是鸟不是飞机。

abstract.en: Picture a bird copied in metal and fuel.
abstract.cn: 想象一只用金属与燃油复刻的鸟。

abstract.en: Imagine a hangar, a runway and a tower as one trade.
abstract.cn: 想象机库、跑道与塔台同属一行。

abstract.en: Think of a licence that lets you leave the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一张让你离开地面的执照。

examples.en: He studied aviation at a technical college.
examples.cn: 他在一所技术学院学航空。

examples.en: Aviation fuel prices rose again.
examples.cn: 航空燃油价格再次上涨。

examples.en: The authority regulates civil aviation.
examples.cn: 该机构监管民用航空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：avi「鸟」（如 aviary 鸟舍）+ -ation「行为、领域」——像鸟一样飞的那门行当，就是 aviation。

root: 拉丁语 avis「鸟」在 1863 年由法语加 -ation 造出 aviation，指空中航行；1903 年动力飞行成功后，词义扩为整个航空产业。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the bird craft: the whole trade of building and running aircraft, and the flying itself sorted by purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是「仿鸟之技」：制造与运营航空器的整个行当，以及按用途划分的飞行本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole trade devoted to leaving the ground
core.cn: 核心意象：一整套让人离开地面的行当

branches.en: A trade employing millions.
branches.cn: 雇用千万人的行当。

branches.en: Fuel, safety and a regulator.
branches.cn: 燃油、安全与监管机构。

branches.en: Private flying under general rules.
branches.cn: 通用规则下的私人飞行。

branches.en: Military flying as one branch.
branches.cn: 作为一支的军事飞行。

branches.en: Both copy what birds do.
branches.cn: 两者都在模仿鸟的所为。

intro.en: Aviation is avi plus -ation; the avi root builds aviator, aviary and avionics, while naut gives aeronautics.
intro.cn: aviation 是 avi 加 -ation；avi 词根构成 aviator、aviary 与 avionics，而 naut 则给出 aeronautics。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is avis, bird, and aviarium, a bird house; Greek nautes, sailor, gives the naut of aeronautics.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 avis「鸟」与 aviarium「鸟舍」；希腊语 nautes「航行者」给出 aeronautics 中的 naut。

definition_zh: 网络安全；保护计算机系统、网络与数据免受攻击、破坏或未经授权访问的实践与领域
definition_en: the practice and field of protecting computer systems, networks and data from attack, damage or unauthorised access
core_image: 银行内网的一块告警面板上，红色标记逐条亮起，值班人员一条条核对来源
scene: 银行内网每天收到大量试探登录，安全团队盯着告警面板逐个处置。 Strong cybersecurity kept the bank's customer records out of the breach.
sceneCN: 这里指保护系统与网络免受攻击的整体工作（第 1 个义项：保护计算机系统与网络免受攻击）；句意为有力的网络安全防护让银行客户记录没有落入泄露事件。图中可辨识物件：告警面板、登录窗口、锁形图标、值班表。

pos.zh: 网络安全；网络空间安全

senses.title: Protecting systems and networks
senses.definition: the work of defending computers, networks and data against unauthorised access, disruption or theft
senses.definitionCN: 保护计算机、网络与数据，防止未经授权的访问、破坏或窃取
senses.example: Strong cybersecurity kept the bank's customer records out of the breach.
senses.exampleCN: 有力的网络安全防护让银行客户记录没有落入泄露事件。
senses.why: Cyber names the networked space and security names freedom from harm, so the word is protection inside that space.
senses.whyCN: 前缀命名联网空间，后一词命名免于伤害，因此这个词就是那个空间内部的保护。

senses.title: The industry and profession
senses.definition: the companies, teams and careers built around defending networks
senses.definitionCN: 围绕网络防御建立的公司、团队与职业
senses.example: The firm hired a cybersecurity team before the product launch.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在产品发布前雇了一支网络安全团队。
senses.why: A defensive practice becomes a trade once the threat is constant enough to pay for.
senses.whyCN: 当威胁持续到值得付费，防御做法就变成一门行业。

senses.title: Defensive measures
senses.definition: the specific controls used to protect a system, such as firewalls, patches and access rules
senses.definitionCN: 用于保护系统的具体控制手段，如防火墙、补丁与访问规则
senses.example: Poor cybersecurity left an old password on the server.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的网络安全措施让服务器上留着一个旧密码。
senses.why: The abstract field is made of concrete measures, and the same word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的领域由具体措施组成，同一个词兼指两者。

senses.title: Defence of an organization
senses.definition: the arrangements by which an institution protects its records, money and services
senses.definitionCN: 机构保护其记录、资金与服务的一整套安排
senses.example: The audit found gaps in the ministry's cybersecurity.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现该部门的网络安全存在缺口。
senses.why: When the protected thing is an institution, the word names a management duty, not only a technology.
senses.whyCN: 当被保护的对象是机构，这个词命名的是一项管理职责，而不只是技术。

senses.title: National policy
senses.definition: the laws, agencies and strategies by which a state protects its networks and infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 国家保护其网络与基础设施的法律、机构与战略
senses.example: The new law treats cybersecurity as part of public safety.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律把网络安全视为公共安全的一部分。
senses.why: Networks cross borders and carry public services, so defence rises from the firm to the state.
senses.whyCN: 网络跨越边界并承载公共服务，防御因此从企业上升到国家。

senses.title: Personal hygiene
senses.definition: the everyday habits by which an individual protects accounts, devices and data
senses.definitionCN: 个人保护账户、设备与数据的日常习惯
senses.example: Good cybersecurity starts with changing a reused password.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的网络安全从改掉重复使用的密码开始。
senses.why: The same defence shrinks to one person's habits, where most breaches actually begin.
senses.whyCN: 同一套防御缩到一个人的习惯上，而多数泄露正是从这里开始。

senses.title: An academic discipline
senses.definition: the study of attacks, defences and risk, taught as a subject with its own methods
senses.definitionCN: 研究攻击、防御与风险的学问，作为一门有自身方法的学科来教授
senses.example: The university added a degree in cybersecurity last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学去年增设了网络安全学位。
senses.why: Once defence has methods and evidence, it can be taught and researched like any other field.
senses.whyCN: 当防御有了方法与证据，它就能像其他领域一样被教授与研究。

senses.title: The threat landscape
senses.definition: the changing set of attackers, methods and vulnerabilities that defenders must track
senses.definitionCN: 防御者必须跟踪的攻击者、手法与漏洞的变动集合
senses.example: Ransomware changed the cybersecurity picture for small clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 勒索软件改变了小诊所的网络安全格局。
senses.why: The word also names the problem, not only the answer, because defence is defined by what it faces.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也命名问题而不只是答案，因为防御由它所面对的东西来定义。

intro.en: Cybersecurity joins cyber-, from cybernetics, coined by Norbert Wiener in 1948 from Greek kybernetes 'steersman', with security, from Latin securitas and securus 'free from care'. The compound became common in the 1990s; the exact first use is source uncertain.
intro.cn: cybersecurity 由 cyber-（源自维纳一九四八年据希腊 kybernetes「舵手」造出的 cybernetics）与 security（拉丁 securitas、securus「无忧」）组合。该复合词在二十世纪九十年代普及；最早用例来源不确定。

items.en: Greek kybernetes meant a steersman or governor, the person who steers a ship and keeps it on course.
items.cn: 希腊 kybernetes 指舵手或掌舵者，即驾驶船只并使其保持航向的人。

items.en: Norbert Wiener used cybernetics for the study of control and communication in animals and machines, taking the Greek steering word.
items.cn: 维纳用 cybernetics 指对动物与机器中控制与通信的研究，取自那个希腊「掌舵」词。

items.en: From the 1960s cyber- was attached to spaces and activities that were networked, giving cyberspace, cybercrime and later cyberattack.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代起，cyber- 被加到联网的空间与活动上，造出网络空间、网络犯罪，后来又造出网络攻击。

items.en: Latin securus meant free from care, built from se- 'without' and cura 'care', and English secure and security come from it.
items.cn: 拉丁 securus 指无忧，由 se-「无」与 cura「忧虑」构成，英语 secure 与 security 由此而来。

items.en: Latin securitas named freedom from danger or care, and English security widened it to protection, guarantees and financial instruments.
items.cn: 拉丁 securitas 指免于危险或忧虑，英语 security 把它扩展到保护、担保与金融工具。

items.en: The two parts were joined in the 1990s as networks became central to business and government; the earliest written use is source uncertain.
items.cn: 两部分在二十世纪九十年代网络成为商业与政府核心时被连起来；最早书面用例来源不确定。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like cybersecurity; the second group names neighbouring ideas in the same field.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「cybersecurity」相近；第二组是同一领域里意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: A prefix or adjective meaning networked or computer-based.
entries.definitionCN: 表示联网或计算机化的前缀或形容词。

entries.definition: The imagined space of networks, built with the same steering prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 由网络构成的想象空间，同用那个「掌舵」前缀。

entries.definition: The study of control and communication, the source of the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 研究控制与通信的学问，是该前缀的来源。

entries.definition: Protection from danger, the second element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 免于危险的保护，是复合词的第二部分。

entries.definition: Crime carried out through networks, the thing this field defends against.
entries.definitionCN: 经网络实施的犯罪，正是这一领域要防御的对象。

entries.definition: Protection of information wherever it is held, whether or not networked.
entries.definitionCN: 保护无论存于何处的信息，不论是否联网。

entries.definition: Protection of the links and traffic between machines.
entries.definitionCN: 保护机器之间的链路与流量。

entries.definition: The ability to keep working and recover after an attack, rather than only to prevent it.
entries.definitionCN: 遭攻击后仍能运作并恢复的能力，而不只是预防。

entries.definition: Active measures to detect and respond to attacks, often in a military or national setting.
entries.definitionCN: 侦测并回应攻击的主动措施，常用于军事或国家语境。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek steering word, the real Latin care word and real policy phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实希腊「掌舵」词、真实拉丁「忧虑」词与真实政策搭配。

normal.en: Cybernetics comes from Greek kybernetes, a steersman, and Norbert Wiener coined it in 1948.
normal.cn: cybernetics 来自希腊 kybernetes「舵手」，由维纳于一九四八年造出。

normal.en: Security comes from Latin securus, free from care, built from se- 'without' and cura 'care'.
normal.cn: security 来自拉丁 securus「无忧」，由 se-「无」与 cura「忧虑」构成。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: cybersecurity threat, policy, firm, awareness, framework.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各支：网络安全威胁、政策、公司、意识、框架。

normal.en: A firewall, a patch and an access rule are all concrete members of the field.
normal.cn: 防火墙、补丁与访问规则都是这一领域的具体成员。

normal.en: The field is defined by what it defends against, so the threat landscape is part of it.
normal.cn: 这一领域由它所防御的东西来定义，因此威胁格局也是它的一部分。

abstract.en: Cybersecurity is a lock on a door that opens onto the whole world.
abstract.cn: 网络安全是装在一扇通向全世界的门上的锁。

abstract.en: The defenders must be right every day; the attacker needs one good night.
abstract.cn: 防御者每天都要做对，攻击者只需要一个好夜晚。

abstract.en: Most breaches begin with one small habit, which is why the field reaches down to individuals.
abstract.cn: 多数泄露始于一个小习惯，这就是这一领域延伸到个人的原因。

examples.en: The hospital increased its cybersecurity budget after a phishing attack.
examples.cn: 在一次钓鱼攻击后，医院增加了网络安全预算。

examples.en: Cybersecurity is now taught in schools as part of digital literacy.
examples.cn: 网络安全如今作为数字素养的一部分在学校教授。

examples.en: A single weak password can defeat years of cybersecurity.
examples.cn: 一个弱密码就能击穿多年的网络安全防护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赛博 + 安全」——网络那片空间里的门锁与巡逻

root: cyber- 源自 cybernetics（维纳一九四八年据希腊 kybernetes「舵手」造出）；security 源自拉丁 securus「无忧」= se- 无 + cura 忧虑。复合词二十世纪九十年代普及，最早用例来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one defence inside a network: protecting systems, an industry, concrete measures, an institution's duty, national policy, personal habits, a discipline, and the threat landscape itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一场网络空间里的防御：保护系统、一个产业、具体措施、机构职责、国家政策、个人习惯、一门学科，以及威胁格局本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bank's warning panel lighting up row by row while an analyst checks each source.
core.cn: 核心意象：银行告警面板逐条亮起，分析员核对每一个来源。

branches.en: THE DEFENCE AND ITS MEASURES: abstract protection is made of firewalls, patches and rules.
branches.cn: 防御与措施：抽象的保护由防火墙、补丁与规则组成。

branches.en: THE TRADE AND THE SCHOOL: constant threat turns defence into a career and then into a taught discipline.
branches.cn: 行业与学堂：持续的威胁把防御变成职业，再变成被教授的学科。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION AND THE STATE: a firm protects its records, and a state protects networks that carry public services.
branches.cn: 机构与国家：企业保护记录，国家保护承载公共服务的网络。

branches.en: THE PERSON: most breaches start with one habit, so the field reaches down to the individual.
branches.cn: 个人：多数泄露始于一个习惯，因此这一领域延伸到个人。

branches.en: THE PROBLEM: the changing set of attackers and weaknesses half-defines the defence.
branches.cn: 问题：不断变化的攻击者与弱点，反过来定义了防御的一半。

intro.en: Cybersecurity joins the Greek steering prefix cyber- with the Latin care word behind security.
intro.cn: cybersecurity 把希腊「掌舵」前缀 cyber- 与 security 背后的拉丁「忧虑」词连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Greek kybernetes gives cybernetics and the prefix cyber-; Latin securus gives secure and security; English joins them into cybersecurity.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 kybernetes 衍生 cybernetics 与前缀 cyber-；拉丁 securus 衍生 secure 与 security；英语把它们连成 cybersecurity。

items.example: The source of the cyber- prefix.

items.exampleCN: 维纳一九四八年的造词。

items.example: The prefix names the space being defended.
items.exampleCN: 前缀命名被防御的空间。
被 se- 否定的名词。

definition_zh: 遗传的；基因的；与起源或发生有关的（旧义）
definition_en: relating to genes or heredity, or, in older use, relating to origin and development
core_image: 两株外观相同的幼苗被切开，内部露出一段段不同的指令条纹
scene: 两株同样的苗，一株在阴处长得细弱，一株在阳光下粗壮。 The difference lies in genetic makeup rather than in care.
sceneCN: 这里 genetic 指「与基因组成有关的」（第 1 个义项：与基因相关的）；句意为差别在于基因组成，而不在于照料。可辨识物件：两株幼苗、遮阴布、光照灯、标注基因组成的卡片。

senses.title: Relating to genes
senses.definition: relating to genes or the material that carries them
senses.definitionCN: 与基因或承载基因的物质相关
senses.example: Genetic testing can reveal carrier status.
senses.exampleCN: 基因检测可以揭示携带者状态。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the whole vocabulary of heredity to a noun, so testing, material and code all become genetic.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把整套遗传词汇附着到名词上，因此检测、物质与密码都可以成为「基因的」。

senses.title: Inherited rather than acquired
senses.definition: determined by inheritance rather than by environment
senses.definitionCN: 由遗传而非环境决定
senses.example: The condition is genetic, not infectious.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病是遗传的，不是传染的。
senses.why: In this sense the word draws a line: what is genetic comes with the organism, not from contact or choice.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，这个词划出一条界线：遗传之物随生物体而来，不来自接触或选择。

senses.title: Relating to origin or development
senses.titleCN: 与起源或发生有关的（旧义）
senses.definition: concerned with the origin and development of something, especially in older philosophy and linguistics
senses.definitionCN: 与某物的起源和发展有关，尤见于较早的哲学与语言学
senses.example: The genetic link between the two languages is disputed.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种语言之间的谱系联系尚有争议。
senses.why: Before genes were known, genetic meant 'pertaining to origins'; linguistics still uses it for language families.
senses.whyCN: 在基因被发现之前，genetic 意为「与起源有关的」；语言学仍用它指语言谱系。

senses.title: Of genetic engineering
senses.definition: relating to the deliberate alteration of genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 与有意改变遗传物质相关
senses.example: Genetic engineering inserted a bacterial gene into the crop.
senses.exampleCN: 基因工程把一个细菌基因植入作物。
senses.why: Once humans could cut and paste sequences, the adjective began to modify the techniques as well as the material.
senses.whyCN: 当人类能够剪切与粘贴序列后，这个形容词开始修饰技术，而不只是物质。

senses.title: Of the genetic code
senses.definition: relating to the mapping from nucleotide triplets to amino acids
senses.definitionCN: 与核苷酸三联体到氨基酸的对应关系相关
senses.example: The genetic code maps triplets to amino acids.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传密码把三联体映射到氨基酸。
senses.why: The word describes a system of correspondence, not a single gene, which is why code is its natural noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述一套对应系统，而非单个基因，因此「密码」是它的自然搭配。

senses.title: Of genetic diversity
senses.definition: relating to the range of genetic variation within a group
senses.definitionCN: 与一个群体内遗传变异的幅度相关
senses.example: Genetic diversity protects a population from disease.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传多样性保护群体免受疾病。
senses.why: Here the adjective measures variety across a group, so it contrasts with uniformity rather than with environment.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词衡量群体内的差异，因此与「一致」相对，而非与环境相对。

senses.title: Of a genetic predisposition
senses.definition: relating to an inherited tendency that raises the likelihood of a condition
senses.definitionCN: 与提高患病可能性的遗传倾向相关
senses.example: A genetic predisposition raises the risk but does not decide it.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传易感性提高风险，但不决定结果。
senses.why: The phrase keeps inheritance and inevitability apart, a distinction the adjective alone does not make.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把遗传与必然分开，而单靠形容词并不能作出这一区分。

senses.title: Of genetic relationship
senses.titleCN: 遗传关系或谱系关系的
senses.definition: relating to shared ancestry, whether of organisms or of languages
senses.definitionCN: 与共同祖先相关，无论指生物还是语言
senses.example: Genetic relationship among species is measured by shared sequences.
senses.exampleCN: 物种间的遗传关系由共享序列来测量。
senses.why: The older 'origin' sense and the newer 'gene' sense meet here: shared ancestry can be read from sequences or from language forms.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「起源」义与较新的「基因」义在此相遇：共同祖先既可从序列读出，也可从语言形式读出。

intro.en: Genetic comes from Greek genetikos 'generative', through French génétique. English first used it for 'pertaining to origin' from 1831, and from the early twentieth century, often dated 1908, for genes and heredity.
intro.cn: genetic 来自希腊 genetikos「生殖的」，经法语 génétique 传入。英语从 1831 年起用它表示「与起源有关的」，到 20 世纪初（常定在 1908 年）才用于基因与遗传。

items.en: Genos 'race, kind, birth' belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-, so the root form is a reconstruction; Latin genus is a cognate, not the source.
items.cn: genos「种族、种类、出生」属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族，因此该词根形式是重构；拉丁 genus 是同源词，并非来源。

items.en: Genetikos 'generative' was built on genesis 'origin' with the adjectival suffix -ikos.
items.cn: genetikos「生殖的」由 genesis「起源」加形容词后缀 -ikos 构成。

items.en: Genetic entered English in 1831 (early nineteenth century) with the sense 'pertaining to origin or development', especially in philosophy and linguistics; the date is recorded, but how the sense developed is not fully documented.
items.cn: genetic 在 1831 年（19 世纪初）以「与起源或发展有关的」义进入英语，尤用于哲学与语言学；年代有记录，但该义如何发展并无完整文献。

items.en: From the early twentieth century, often dated 1908, the adjective was attached to genes and heredity, and this sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪初（常定在 1908 年），这个形容词被附着到基因与遗传上，这一义项如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: Latin genus and generare belong to the same PIE family, but genetic is not derived from them; generic is the adjective built directly on Latin genus.
items.cn: 拉丁 genus 与 generare 属于同一原始印欧语词族，但 genetic 并非由它们派生；generic 才是直接建立在拉丁 genus 上的形容词。

items.en: Source uncertain (sense dates): the 1831 first use is on record, but the exact date of the biological shift is given variously as 1905 and 1908, and no Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（义项年代）：1831 年的首用有记录，但生物学义的确切年代有 1905 与 1908 两说；且 genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

note.en: Group one separates genetic from related formations and near sound-alikes; group two separates it from the words for inherited and whole-genome properties.
note.cn: 第一组把 genetic 与相关构词及音近词分开；第二组把它与「遗传的」「全基因组的」等词区分。

entries.definition: Built directly on Latin genus 'kind', not on Greek genetikos: it means 'general, not branded or specific'. The two words are related only through the PIE family.
entries.definitionCN: 直接建立在拉丁 genus「种类」上，而非希腊 genetikos：意为「通用的、非专属的」。两词仅通过原始印欧语词族相关联。

entries.definition: An older adjective form now mostly replaced by genetic; it survives in some technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词形式，现多被 genetic 取代；仍残存于部分技术文献。

entries.definition: From genitalis, built on the same gignere stem, but it refers to reproduction and anatomy, not to genes.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 genitalis，建立在同一 gignere 词干上，但指生殖与解剖，而非基因。

entries.definition: Con- 'together' plus gignere 'beget': present from birth. It is not a synonym of genetic, since a congenital cause may be non-genetic.
entries.definitionCN: con-「共同」加 gignere「生育」：指出生即有。它不是 genetic 的同义词，因为先天原因未必是遗传原因。

entries.definition: It stresses descent from ancestors, while genetic points to the genes that carry the trait.
entries.definitionCN: 强调从祖先传来，而 genetic 指向承载性状的基因。

entries.definition: The ordinary participle from inherit; genetic is the technical adjective and can also mean 'relating to genes' without transmission.
entries.definitionCN: inherit 的普通分词；genetic 是技术形容词，也可仅指「与基因有关」而不涉及传递。

entries.definition: Relating to the entire genome rather than to individual genes.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个基因组相关，而非单个基因。

entries.definition: Present at birth, whether or not the cause is genetic; the two words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生时即存在，无论原因是否遗传；两词回答不同问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genos 'kind' + -ic: belonging to the kind one is born into.
normal.cn: genos「种类」+ -ic：属于出生所在的那个种类。

normal.en: The family runs gene, genetic, genetically, genetics and geneticist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gene、genetic、genetically、genetics 与 geneticist。

normal.en: Old sense: genetic philosophy, genetic linguistics, meaning 'of origins'.
normal.cn: 旧义搭配：发生哲学、谱系语言学，意为「关于起源的」。

normal.en: New sense in the early twentieth century: genetic code, genetic testing, genetic engineering.
normal.cn: 20 世纪初的新义搭配：遗传密码、基因检测、基因工程。

normal.en: Genetic is not congenital: a congenital condition need not be genetic.
normal.cn: genetic 不等于 congenital：先天状况未必是遗传的。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed envelope that comes with the body and cannot be exchanged.
abstract.cn: 想象一个随身体附来的密封信封，无法退换。

abstract.en: Picture two identical chairs made from different batches of wood.
abstract.cn: 想象两把相同的椅子，用不同批次的木材做成。

abstract.en: Picture an old map labelled by origin rather than by road.
abstract.cn: 想象一张按起源而非按道路标注的旧地图。

examples.en: Genetic testing is offered to families with a known history of the disease.
examples.cn: 有明确家族史的家庭可获得基因检测。

examples.en: The two languages show a genetic relationship in their verb endings.
examples.cn: 这两种语言在动词词尾上显示出谱系关系。

examples.en: Genetic diversity fell sharply after the population crashed.
examples.cn: 群体数量骤降后，遗传多样性急剧下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: gene（基因）+ tic（形容词尾）——与基因有关的 → 遗传的；旧义是「关于起源的」。

root: 希腊 genetikos「生殖的」← genesis「起源」+ genos「种族、种类」；genos 出自原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式）；拉丁 genus 为同源词，非来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective as it moves from origins to genes: gene-related, inherited, origin-related, engineered, coded, diverse, predisposing and ancestry-sharing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形容词从「起源」走向「基因」：与基因相关、遗传而来、关于起源、经工程改造、关于密码、关于多样性、关于易感性、关于共同祖先。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical seedlings cut open to show different stripes of instructions inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：两株外观相同的幼苗被切开，内部露出不同的指令条纹。

branches.en: GENES AND INHERITANCE: the core modern pair, what genes are and what comes with them.
branches.cn: 基因与遗传：现代核心的两项，基因是什么，以及随基因而来的东西。

branches.en: ORIGINS AND ANCESTRY: the older sense survives in language families and shared descent.
branches.cn: 起源与祖先：旧义残存于语系与共同世系。

branches.en: ENGINEERING AND CODE: techniques for altering sequences, and the mapping they use.
branches.cn: 工程与密码：改变序列的技术，以及它们所用的对应表。

branches.en: DIVERSITY: variation across a group, measured at the level of genes.
branches.cn: 多样性：群体内的变异，在基因层面测量。

branches.en: PREDISPOSITION: an inherited tendency that raises risk without fixing the outcome.
branches.cn: 易感性：提高风险却不固定结果的遗传倾向。

intro.en: Genetic is the adjective of the Greek-derived gen- family; its suffix marks relation, and the same stem builds the science and the agent noun.
intro.cn: genetic 是希腊来源 gen- 词族的形容词；后缀标记关系，同一词干还构成学科名与从业者名。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos 'race, kind' gives genetic and genetics; -ikos gives the adjective, -ics the science. No Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty; Latin genus is only a cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos「种族、种类」衍生 genetic 与 genetics；-ikos 构成形容词，-ics 构成学科名。genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空；拉丁 genus 仅为同源词。

items.example: The stem names a kind that reproduces itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名自我繁衍的「类」。

items.example: Genesis supplies the idea of coming into being.
items.exampleCN: genesis 提供「进入存在」的观念。
这个形容词描述能生成之物。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: A gene is a unit of heredity.

items.exampleCN: 这些菌株在遗传上不同。
这位遗传学家绘制了该区域。

definition_zh: n. 猿；类人猿（无尾）；笨拙的模仿者　v. 模仿；照搬（常含贬义）
definition_en: A large tailless primate such as a gorilla or chimpanzee; as a verb, to copy someone's behaviour or style closely and rather clumsily, usually with a hint of criticism.
core_image: 没有尾巴的大猿，以及照着别人动作硬学一遍
scene: 小猩猩照着饲养员的动作把毛巾搭在肩上。 The young chimp likes to ape the keeper's gestures.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：动词 ape 指照着别人的样子笨拙模仿，多半带一点贬义。

pos.zh: 猿；类人猿；笨拙的模仿者

derivatives.zh: 像猿一样地；笨拙模仿地

senses.title: A tailless primate
senses.definition: a large primate without a tail, such as a gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan or gibbon
senses.definitionCN: 没有尾巴的大型灵长类动物，如大猩猩、黑猩猩、红毛猩猩或长臂猿
senses.example: The great apes share most of their DNA with humans.
senses.exampleCN: 类人猿与人类共享大部分 DNA。
senses.why: The key contrast with a monkey is the tail: apes have none, and that single feature is what the noun picks out.
senses.whyCN: 与 monkey 的关键区别在尾巴：猿没有尾巴，这个名词抓住的正是这一条特征。

senses.title: To copy clumsily
senses.definition: to imitate someone's actions, voice or style closely, often without understanding, and usually with a disapproving tone
senses.definitionCN: 紧紧照着他人的动作、声音或风格去模仿，往往并不理解，语气多含贬义
senses.example: The band spent a year aping their heroes before finding a voice.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队照搬偶像整整一年，才找到自己的声音。
senses.why: Apes were long thought to mimic human gestures, so the animal name turned into a verb for shallow copying.
senses.whyCN: 人们长期认为猿会模仿人的动作，于是这个动物名变成了表示浅层照搬的动词。

senses.title: A crude imitator
senses.definition: a person who copies others without originality, or who behaves in a rough, foolish way
senses.definitionCN: 毫无原创性地照搬他人的人，或举止粗鲁愚笨的人
senses.example: He was dismissed as an ape of better painters.
senses.exampleCN: 他被看作只会照搬更优秀画家的人而不受重视。
senses.why: This sense keeps both halves of the word at once: the animal and the copying, aimed at a person as an insult.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项同时保留了词的两半：动物与模仿，用作针对人的贬称。

intro.en: Ape is a native Germanic word, Old English apa, related to Dutch aap and German Affe. The verb sense grew out of the belief that apes mimic people.
intro.cn: ape 是日耳曼本族词，古英语作 apa，与荷兰语 aap、德语 Affe 同源。动词义来自「猿会模仿人」这一观念。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic root is apan-, a word for the large tailless primates known in northern Europe.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼词根是 apan-，指北欧人所知的大型无尾灵长类动物。

items.en: Old English wrote apa for both the animal and, loosely, a fool. The plural was apan.
items.cn: 古英语用 apa 指这种动物，也宽泛地指愚人，复数作 apan。

items.en: Middle English ape kept the animal sense and added the figurative use for someone who copies others.
items.cn: 中古英语 ape 保留动物义，并增加了「照搬他人者」的比喻用法。

items.en: Dutch aap and German Affe are the same word, which shows the term is Germanic rather than borrowed from Latin.
items.cn: 荷兰语 aap 与德语 Affe 是同一个词，说明它是日耳曼词，而非从拉丁语借来。

items.en: Around the 1630s the noun became a verb meaning to mimic, from the popular idea that apes imitate human gestures.
items.cn: 1630 年代前后，名词转动词，意为「模仿」，源自「猿会学人的动作」这一流行观念。

items.en: Modern biology keeps ape for the tailless group, separating it sharply from monkey, which normally has a tail.
items.cn: 现代生物学把 ape 留给无尾类群，与通常有尾的 monkey 明确区分。

note.en: The look-alike group guards against apt and ace, which are only a letter away; the near-meaning group lists verbs for copying.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只差一个字母的 apt、ace 混淆；近义组列出表示「模仿」的动词。

entries.definition: Suitable, or quick to learn.
A top player, or the highest card.
A sleeveless cloak, or a headland.
Foolishly imitative.
To copy a voice or manner closely.
entries.definitionCN: 逼真地模仿声音或举止。

entries.definition: To do the same as someone else.
To copy in order to match or beat.
To repeat words without thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 不动脑子地重复别人的话。

normalIntro.en: Ape has three letters and no tail: apes are the primates that lost the tail, monkeys kept it.
normalIntro.cn: ape 只有三个字母，也没有尾巴：猿是没尾巴的那一类，猴子留着尾巴。

normal.en: Great apes are gorillas, chimps, orangutans and gibbons.
normal.cn: 类人猿包括大猩猩、黑猩猩、红毛猩猩与长臂猿。

normal.en: The verb is disapproving: aping is copying without thought.
normal.cn: 动词含贬义：aping 是不动脑地照搬。

normal.en: Inflections are apes, aped, aping, with no doubled letter.
normal.cn: 变化形式是 apes、aped、aping，不双写字母。

normal.en: Do not confuse ape with apt, which means suitable.
normal.cn: 别把 ape 与 apt「恰当的」混淆。

normal.en: The adjective apish describes foolish imitation.
normal.cn: 形容词 apish 形容愚蠢的模仿。

abstract.en: Picture a chimp copying a keeper's wave.
abstract.cn: 想象黑猩猩学饲养员挥手。

abstract.en: Imagine a band sounding exactly like its heroes.
abstract.cn: 想象一支乐队听起来和偶像一模一样。

abstract.en: Think of a mirror that only repeats, never adds.
abstract.cn: 想象一面只会重复、从不添东西的镜子。

examples.en: Gibbons are the smallest of the apes.
examples.cn: 长臂猿是猿类中体型最小的。

examples.en: He aped his teacher's accent for a laugh.
examples.cn: 他学老师的口音逗大家笑。

examples.en: The film is aping a style it never understands.
examples.cn: 这部电影照搬了一种它并不理解的风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ape 三个字母，尾巴也「没有」——无尾的是 ape，有尾的是 monkey；动词就是照搬别人的动作。

root: 日耳曼本族词，古英语 apa「猿」，与荷兰语 aap、德语 Affe 同源；因古人认为猿善学人动作，1630 年代生出动词「模仿、照搬」，再引申指拙劣的模仿者。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses run from the animal to the copying: a tailless primate, the act of copying like one, and a person who only copies.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从动物走向模仿：无尾的大猿，像猿一样照搬的动作，以及只会照搬的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a big tailless ape, and a clumsy run at someone else's moves
core.cn: 核心意象：没有尾巴的大猿，以及照着别人动作硬学一遍

branches.en: A gorilla with no tail at all.
branches.cn: 完全没有尾巴的大猩猩。

branches.en: A gibbon swinging through the canopy.
branches.cn: 在树冠间摆荡的长臂猿。

branches.en: A chimp copying a keeper's wave.
branches.cn: 学饲养员挥手的小黑猩猩。

branches.en: A painter who only repeats others.
branches.cn: 只会重复别人的画家。

branches.en: Both copy without adding anything.
branches.cn: 两者都只是照搬，不加新东西。

intro.en: Ape itself has no affixes, but it takes -ish and -like, and the copying idea is carried by the Latin roots mim- and imit-.
intro.cn: ape 本身不带词缀，但可加 -ish 与 -like；「模仿」这一概念由拉丁词根 mim- 与 imit- 承载。

latinIntro.en: Ape is Germanic, so the classical layer belongs to its synonyms: Latin mimus and imitari, and similis for likeness.
latinIntro.cn: ape 是日耳曼词，所以古典层次属于它的近义词：拉丁语 mimus、imitari，以及表示相似的 similis。

definition_zh: n. 仲裁人，公断人；（引申）最终裁定者
definition_en: An independent person appointed to hear a dispute and give a decision that the parties have agreed to accept; by extension, anyone whose judgement settles a question.
core_image: 坐在两造中间、最后拍板的那个人
scene: 双方各让一步，接受了仲裁人的裁定。 Both sides accepted the arbitrator's ruling.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arbitrator 指被指定来听审并裁断争议的中立第三方。

pos.zh: 仲裁人；公断人；最终裁定者

senses.title: The appointed decider
senses.definition: a neutral person chosen by the parties, or by a body, to hear evidence and impose a settlement
senses.definitionCN: 由双方或某机构选定的中立者，听取证据并作出有约束力的解决方案
senses.example: The union and the firm could not agree on an arbitrator.
senses.exampleCN: 工会与公司无法就仲裁人人选达成一致。
senses.why: The ending -or marks the doer, so arbitrator is simply the one who arbitrates, the person inside the process.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -or 标记施动者，所以 arbitrator 就是「做仲裁的那个人」，是程序里的那个人。

senses.title: The final authority on a question
senses.definition: by extension, a person or thing whose judgement is treated as settling a matter of taste or value
senses.definitionCN: 引申指其判断被视为能定论品味或价值问题的人或事物
senses.example: Time is the only arbitrator of literary reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 时间是文学声誉唯一的裁定者。
senses.why: The legal role is borrowed as a metaphor: whoever ends the argument occupies the middle chair, even with no contract.
senses.whyCN: 法律角色被借作比喻：谁能终止争论，谁就坐上了中间那把椅子，哪怕并无合同。

intro.en: Arbitrator is the Latin agent noun from arbitrari, to judge, itself from arbiter, a witness who goes to see. English took both arbiter and arbitrator.
intro.cn: arbitrator 是拉丁语 arbitrari「裁断」的施动名词，而 arbitrari 出自 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」。英语把 arbiter 与 arbitrator 都吸收了。

items.en: Arbiter meant a witness who goes to look and then judges, from ad-, to, plus baetere, to come.
items.cn: arbiter 指前去看情况再作判断的见证人，由 ad-「向」加 baetere「来」构成。

items.en: The verb arbitrari meant to weigh a matter and decide it, the neutral ancestor of both English words.
items.cn: 动词 arbitrari 意为「权衡并裁定」，是两个英语词的中性祖先。

items.en: Adding -or, the doer ending, gave arbitrator, the person who performs the judging.
items.cn: 加上表施动者的 -or 得到 arbitrator，即执行裁断的那个人。

items.en: Anglo-French legal writing spelled it arbitratour, the form English courts used in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语法律文献拼作 arbitratour，这是 14 世纪末英国法院使用的形式。

items.en: English kept both forms: arbiter for any decisive authority, arbitrator for the appointed legal role.
items.cn: 英语保留了两种形式：arbiter 泛指有定论权的权威，arbitrator 专指被指定的法律角色。

items.en: Today an arbitrator is named in the clause, and the award carries the force of a court judgement.
items.cn: 如今仲裁人在条款中被指定，其裁决具有法院判决的效力。

note.en: The look-alike group separates arbiter, the wider word, from arbitrator, the appointed role, and warns against arbitrary; the near-meaning group lists other neutral deciders.
note.cn: 形近组把泛指的 arbiter 与专任的 arbitrator 分开，并提醒别与 arbitrary 混淆；近义组列出其他中立裁断者。

entries.definition: Anyone with power to decide.
To judge between two sides.
Decided by whim, not reason.
One who helps sides agree.
A person who gives a formal ruling.
An official who enforces the rules.
An official who settles play.
One who judges value or quality.

normalIntro.en: Arbitrator is arbitrate plus -or: the person who does the arbitrating, sitting in the middle chair.
normalIntro.cn: arbitrator 就是 arbitrate 加 -or：做仲裁的那个人，坐在中间那把椅子上。

normal.en: Arbitrator is the appointed role; arbiter is the wider word.
normal.cn: arbitrator 是专任角色，arbiter 是泛指说法。

normal.en: A mediator only helps; an arbitrator decides.
normal.cn: mediator 只帮谈，arbitrator 直接定。

normal.en: The decision is an award, and it binds the parties.
normal.cn: 裁定叫 award，对双方有约束力。

normal.en: Sole arbitrator means one person, not a panel.
normal.cn: sole arbitrator 指独任一人，不是小组。

normal.en: Do not mix arbitrator with arbitrary, which means capricious.
normal.cn: 别把 arbitrator 与 arbitrary「反复无常」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a third chair between two arguing sides.
abstract.cn: 想象争执双方之间的第三把椅子。

abstract.en: Imagine a signature that ends a two-year quarrel.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名结束两年争吵。

abstract.en: Think of time as the judge nobody appointed.
abstract.cn: 想象时间这位没人指定的裁判。

examples.en: The arbitrator heard both sides for three days.
examples.cn: 仲裁人听双方陈述听了三天。

examples.en: Two arbitrators were replaced for a conflict of interest.
examples.cn: 两名仲裁人因利益冲突被更换。

examples.en: She acted as sole arbitrator in the shipping dispute.
examples.cn: 她在这起航运争议中担任独任仲裁人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arbitrate「仲裁」+ -or「人」——做仲裁的那个人，就是 arbitrator。

root: 拉丁语 arbiter「前去查看的见证人」生出 arbitrari「裁断」，加施动后缀 -or 成 arbitrator「裁断者」；英语 14 世纪末吸收，与泛指的 arbiter 分工并存。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the middle chair: the person appointed to end a dispute, and anyone whose word ends an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是中间那把椅子：被指定来终结争议的人，以及一句话就能终结争论的任何人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person seated between the two sides who makes the final call
core.cn: 核心意象：坐在两造中间、最后拍板的那个人

branches.en: A neutral named in the clause.
branches.cn: 条款中指定的中立者。

branches.en: Three days of hearing both sides.
branches.cn: 听双方陈述的三天。

branches.en: Time judging literary reputation.
branches.cn: 裁定文学声誉的时间。

branches.en: A critic whose word ends debate.
branches.cn: 一句话终止争论的评论家。

branches.en: Both occupy the middle chair.
branches.cn: 两者都坐在中间那把椅子上。

intro.en: Arbitrator is arbitrate plus the doer suffix -or, the same ending that builds actor, mediator and adjudicator.
intro.cn: arbitrator 是 arbitrate 加施动后缀 -or，同一词尾还构成 actor、mediator 与 adjudicator。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arbiter, arbitrari and the agent noun arbitrator; -or is the Latin doer ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arbiter、arbitrari 与施动名词 arbitrator；-or 是拉丁语的施动者词尾。

latinEntries.example: Arbiter is the base of the family.

definition_zh: v. 为（他人或自己所受的伤害）报仇；替……复仇
definition_en: To inflict punishment in return for a wrong done to oneself or to another person.
core_image: 替倒下的人把那一击还回去
scene: 他发誓要替被害的兄弟报仇。 He swore to avenge his murdered brother.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：avenge 指为他人所受的伤害而施加惩罚，宾语通常是受害者或那桩伤害。

senses.title: Punish a wrong for someone
senses.titleCN: 替他人所受的伤害施加惩罚
senses.definition: to take or exact punishment for a harm suffered by another person or by oneself
senses.definitionCN: 为他人或自己所受的伤害而施加或索取惩罚
senses.example: They raised an army to avenge the raid.
senses.exampleCN: 他们集结军队为那次袭击复仇。
senses.why: Avenge is a- plus venge, from Latin vindicare, to claim or punish, so it directs a claim of justice at a wrong.
senses.whyCN: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，出自拉丁语 vindicare「索还、惩罚」，因此它把一份正义诉求指向那桩伤害。

senses.title: Reflexive retaliation
senses.definition: in a reflexive pattern with on, to pay back a personal injury by harming the offender
senses.definitionCN: 用于带 on 的反身句式，指以伤害冒犯者来回报自身所受的损害
senses.example: He avenged himself on the men who cheated him.
senses.exampleCN: 他向那些骗过他的人复仇。
senses.why: The reflexive keeps the injured party in view, which is what separates avenge from revenge in careful use.
senses.whyCN: 反身式让受害者始终在视野之中，这正是严谨用法中 avenge 与 revenge 的分界。

intro.en: Avenge is a- plus venge, from Old French avengier, from Latin vindicare, to lay claim to or punish, from vindex, a claimant or avenger.
intro.cn: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，出自古法语 avengier，源自拉丁语 vindicare「索还、惩罚」，而 vindicare 出自 vindex「索求者、复仇者」。

items.en: A root meaning to point out or claim stands behind words of showing and demanding.
items.cn: 一个表示「指出、索求」的词根支撑着显示与要求类的词。

items.en: Latin vindex named a claimant, one who demands a thing back or answers for a wrong.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vindex 指索求者，即索回某物或为不公讨回公道的人。

items.en: From it vindicare meant to lay claim to, to set free, and to punish.
items.cn: 由此 vindicare 意为「索还、释放、惩罚」。

items.en: Old French venger kept the punishing side, to take vengeance for a harm.
items.cn: 古法语 venger 保留了惩罚一面，即为伤害复仇。

items.en: Adding a-, to, gave avengier, to direct that punishment at a wrong.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」构成 avengier，即把惩罚指向某桩伤害。

items.en: Middle English avengen entered in the fourteenth century and displaced older native words.
items.cn: 中古英语 avengen 于十四世纪进入，取代了更早的本族词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the venge family; the near-meaning group lists other words for paying back a wrong.
note.cn: 形近组保留 venge 词族；近义组列出其他表示回报伤害的词。

normalIntro.cn: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，与 vengeance 同族：把回报瞄准某人所受的伤害。

normal.en: Avenge takes the victim or the wrong as object.
normal.cn: avenge 的宾语是受害者或那桩伤害。

root: 拉丁语 vindex「索求者」生出 vindicare「索还、惩罚」，古法语 venger 加 a-「向」成 avengier，入中古英语作 avengen，即 avenge「为……复仇」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses aim punishment at a wrong: for another person or oneself, and in the reflexive pattern against the offender.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都把惩罚指向一桩伤害：为他人或自己所受的伤害，以及在反身句式中指向冒犯者。

definition_zh: n. 女校友；女毕业生（复数 alumnae）
definition_en: A female former student or graduate of a school, college or university; the plural form is alumnae.
core_image: 毕业多年后仍被母校叫作「养女」的那个人
scene: 她毕业二十年，每年校庆都坐在第一排。 The college honoured its oldest alumna at the ceremony.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：她是从这所学院毕业的女性，所以用 alumna 而不是 alumnus。校方在校庆上向这位最年长的女校友致敬。

senses.title: A female graduate
senses.definition: a woman who formerly studied at a particular school, college or university
senses.definitionCN: 曾在某所学校、学院或大学就读的女性
senses.example: She is an alumna of the medical school.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这所医学院的女校友。
senses.why: Latin alumnus meant a foster child or pupil, one nourished by a household; the -a ending marks the feminine, so the school is still pictured as a foster mother.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alumnus 意为养子或学生，即被一个家庭养育的人；-a 词尾标示阴性，因此学校仍被想象为养母。

senses.title: In institutional records
senses.definition: used by colleges in titles, lists and fundraising to identify women on the graduate roll
senses.definitionCN: 高校在头衔、名录与募捐中用以标识毕业生名册上的女性
senses.example: The alumnae fund paid for two new scholarships.
senses.exampleCN: 女校友基金资助了两项新奖学金。
senses.why: Institutions keep the Latin plurals because their rolls are formal documents, so alumnae appears where speech would simply say alums.
senses.whyCN: 院校保留拉丁语复数，因为名录属于正式文件，所以在口语只说 alums 的地方，书面仍写 alumnae。

intro.en: Alumna is the feminine of Latin alumnus, a foster child or pupil, from alere, to nourish. The school is imagined as the household that fed you, and the ending tells the gender.
intro.cn: alumna 是拉丁语 alumnus 的阴性形式，alumnus 意为养子或学生，来自 alere「滋养」。学校被想象为喂养过你的那个家，词尾则标示性别。

items.en: Latin alere meant to nourish, feed or bring up. The same root gives aliment, alimentary and, through altus, altitude.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alere 意为「滋养、喂养、养育」。同一词根产生 aliment、alimentary，并经 altus 产生 altitude。

items.en: Alumnus was the noun for a foster son or pupil, literally one who is nourished. A teacher or a school stood in the place of a parent.
items.cn: alumnus 是表示养子或学生的名词，字面为「被养育的人」。老师或学校站在父母的位置上。

items.en: Alumna is the feminine singular and alumnae the feminine plural, while alumnus and alumni are the masculine pair. English borrowed all four intact.
items.cn: alumna 是阴性单数，alumnae 是阴性复数，而 alumnus 与 alumni 是阳性的一对。英语把四个形式整套借入。

items.en: English took alumnus in the seventeenth century and alumna later, as women began to keep their own graduate rolls at colleges.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 alumnus，alumna 较晚，随着女性开始在高校拥有自己的毕业生名册而通行。

items.en: Today alum serves for any gender in speech, while formal writing still separates alumna, alumnae, alumnus and alumni.
items.cn: 如今口语中 alum 不分性别通用，而正式书面语仍区分 alumna、alumnae、alumnus 与 alumni。

abstract.en: Imagine a school still setting a place at the table for her.

examples.cn: 每位女校友都收到了百年校庆的邀请。

examples.en: The alumnae gathered in the old library.

examples.en: She is a proud alumna of a small state college.

definition_zh: adj. 利他的；无私的；为他人利益着想的
definition_en: Showing a selfless concern for the welfare of others; motivated by the good of other people rather than by personal gain.
core_image: 把好处推给别人，自己退到后面
scene: 他把奖金全捐给了病房里的孩子，自己一分没留。 His altruistic gesture surprised the whole office.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：他把奖金捐出去，不为自己留任何好处。这种把他人利益放在前面的做法，就是 altruistic 所说的利他。

forms.label: 无 -er/-est 形式（多音节形容词，用 more/most）

senses.title: Putting others first
senses.definition: motivated by the good of other people rather than by any benefit to oneself
senses.definitionCN: 以他人的好处而非自身所得为出发点的
senses.example: Her altruistic choice cost her a year of savings.
senses.exampleCN: 她这个利他的选择让她损失了一年的积蓄。
senses.why: The base is Latin alter, the other of two, so the word literally points away from the self and toward the other person.
senses.whyCN: 词根是拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」，所以这个词字面上就把手从自己指向了他人。

senses.title: In biology and ethics
senses.titleCN: 生物学与伦理学中的利他
senses.definition: describing behaviour that lowers the fitness or payoff of the actor while raising that of another
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述降低行动者自身适合度或收益、却提高他人收益的行为
senses.example: Altruistic grooming is common among related bats.
senses.exampleCN: 利他性的相互梳理在亲缘蝙蝠中很常见。
senses.why: Comte coined the noun as the opposite of egoism, and the sciences kept that strict sense: a real cost to the giver, a real gain to the receiver.
senses.whyCN: 孔德把这个名词造出来作为利己主义的反面，各门学科保留了这一严格含义：给予者确有损失，接受者确有收益。

intro.en: Altruistic is the adjective of altruism, a word Auguste Comte coined in French around 1830 from autrui, other people, which descends from Latin alter, the other of two.
intro.cn: altruistic 是 altruism 的形容词，而 altruism 是孔德约 1830 年在法语中造的词，来自 autrui「他人」，后者又源自拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」。

items.en: Latin alter meant the other of two. It is the base of the whole family: alternate, alternative and the phrase alter ego.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alter 意为「两者中的另一个」。它是整个词族的底座：alternate、alternative 以及短语 alter ego。

items.en: Old French autrui, other people, grew out of a Latin form built on alter, with the l turning into a u sound on the way.
items.cn: 古法语 autrui「他人」由建立在 alter 之上的拉丁语形式发展而来，途中 l 变成了 u 音。

items.en: Auguste Comte coined French altruisme around 1830 from autrui, pairing it against egoisme to name the principle of living for others.
items.cn: 孔德约 1830 年由 autrui 造出法语 altruisme，与 egoisme 相对，用来命名「为他人而活」的原则。

items.en: English took altruism in the mid nineteenth century, and George Henry Lewes spread it through his writing on Comte and positivism.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪中期借入 altruism，刘易斯通过介绍孔德与实证主义的著作把它推广开来。

items.en: Altruistic is the adjective built with -istic, now standard in ethics, psychology, evolutionary biology and ordinary praise of a generous act.
items.cn: altruistic 是用 -istic 构成的形容词，如今在伦理学、心理学、演化生物学以及对慷慨行为的日常称赞中都是标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the altru- family and the -istic ending; the near-meaning group lists other words for putting others first.
note.cn: 形近组保留 altru- 词族与 -istic 词尾；近义组列出其他表示「把他人放在前面」的词。

normal.en: Alter means other, so altruistic means other-first.

normal.en: It is the opposite of egoistic, and Comte designed the pair.

normal.en: Do not confuse altruistic with authentic: one is about others, one about truth.

abstract.en: Imagine a hand giving away the whole loaf and keeping the crumbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把整条面包送出去，只留下碎屑。

abstract.cn: 想象一只蝙蝠为再也见不到的表亲梳理毛发。

examples.en: His altruistic motives were never in doubt.
examples.cn: 他的利他动机从未受到怀疑。

examples.en: The donation was purely altruistic, with no tax benefit.

examples.en: She acted altruistically and asked for nothing back.

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱他如实」——爱他（altru）如实（istic）：实实在在地爱别人、不图回报，就是利他的、无私的。

root: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」经古法语 autrui「他人」，由孔德造出 altruisme，英语借为 altruism「利他主义」，再加 -istic 构成形容词 altruistic，字面即「把他人放在自己之前」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same outward turn: everyday praise for a generous motive, and the technical label for behaviour that costs the giver.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次向外的转身：日常里对慷慨动机的称赞，以及学术上对「给予者付出代价」的行为的标注。

definition_en: A small emblem worn to show rank, membership or achievement; a mark taken as a sign of something.
core_image: 别在胸前说明你是谁的那小块金属
scene: 保安别好徽章，站到闸机旁边。 The guard pinned on his badge and stood by the gate.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：badge 指佩戴以表明身份、职级或归属的小徽记。

senses.title: A worn emblem
senses.definition: a small piece of metal, cloth or plastic worn to show rank, job or membership
senses.definitionCN: 佩戴的金属、布或塑料小件，用以表明职级、工作或归属
senses.example: Show your badge at the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 在前台出示你的徽章。
senses.why: Badge began as a heraldic mark identifying a follower of a noble house, so it always answers who you belong to.
senses.whyCN: badge 起初是标识某贵族门下随从的纹章标记，因此它始终回答「你属于谁」。

senses.title: A sign of a quality
senses.definition: a thing taken as evidence of a quality or achievement, whether worn or not
senses.definitionCN: 被视为某种品质或成就之凭证的事物，无论是否佩戴
senses.example: He wore his scars as a badge of courage.
senses.exampleCN: 他把伤疤当作勇气的象征。
senses.why: Because the worn mark proved membership, any proof of a quality could be called a badge.
senses.whyCN: 因为佩戴的标记证明了归属，任何品质的凭证也就都能称为 badge。

senses.title: A small screen marker
senses.definition: in computing, a small number or icon attached to another icon to signal pending items
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机界面中，附于另一图标之上的小数字或小图标，用以提示待处理项
senses.example: A red badge showed nine unread messages.
senses.exampleCN: 一个红色角标显示有九条未读消息。
senses.why: The screen borrowed the worn mark for the same job: a small sign that tells you something waits.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕借用了佩戴标记来做同一件事：一个小提示，告诉你有东西在等着。

intro.en: Badge comes from Middle English bage, a distinguishing mark, whose earlier origin is unknown; it first named the emblem of a noble household.
intro.cn: badge 来自中古英语 bage「识别标记」，更早的来源不明；它最初指贵族门第的徽记。

items.en: Bage is recorded in the fourteenth century for a mark worn by a servant of a lord.
items.cn: bage 于十四世纪有记载，指领主仆从佩戴的标记。

items.en: Such marks identified retainers and were often made of cheap metal in quantity.
items.cn: 这类标记用以识别随从，常以廉价金属大量制作。

items.en: Armies adopted badges of rank and of regiment, fixing the modern shape.
items.cn: 军队采用军衔与团队徽章，确立了现代形态。

items.en: Scouting and schools used badges for skills earned, widening the sense.
items.cn: 童子军与学校用徽章表示已获得的技能，扩展了词义。

items.en: The phrase badge of honour made the word a general sign of a quality.
items.cn: 「荣誉的象征」这一短语使该词成为品质的通用标志。

items.en: Software adopted badge for the small counter attached to an app icon.
items.cn: 软件采用 badge 指附于应用图标上的小计数标记。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words of similar shape; the near-meaning group lists other words for a small identifying sign.
note.cn: 形近组保留形状相近的词；近义组列出表示小型识别标志的其他词。

entries.definition: A burrowing animal, or to pester.
A strip of cloth for a wound.
To move slightly, or to yield.
To get something by begging.
A design standing for a group.
Marks of rank or office.
A thing standing for something else.
A metal disc given for merit.

normalIntro.en: Badge began as the mark of a lord’s follower, so it always says who you belong to or what you have earned.
normalIntro.cn: badge 起初是领主随从的标记，因此它总在说明你属于谁、或你赢得了什么。

normal.en: A badge of honour is the set phrase.
normal.cn: a badge of honour 是固定短语。

normal.en: Name badge and identity badge are workplace terms.
normal.cn: name badge 与 identity badge 是职场用语。

normal.en: Emblem is the design, badge the object.
normal.cn: emblem 指图案，badge 指物件。

normal.en: Insignia is usually plural in use.
normal.cn: insignia 在使用中多为复数。

normal.en: Apps use badge for the little counter.
normal.cn: 应用用 badge 指那个小计数。

abstract.en: Picture a small disc pinned over a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象别在口袋上方的小圆牌。

abstract.en: Imagine a scar read as proof.
abstract.cn: 想象一道被当作凭证的伤疤。

abstract.en: Think of a red dot that will not go away.
abstract.cn: 想象一个怎么也不消失的红点。

examples.en: Her badge gave her access to the lab.
examples.cn: 她的徽章让她能进入实验室。

examples.en: They earned a badge for first aid.
examples.cn: 他们因急救技能获得一枚徽章。

examples.en: The app badge showed three alerts.
examples.cn: 应用角标显示有三条提醒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音记忆：读作「拜纸」——别在胸前那张说明身份的小牌，就是 badge；引申为「象征」，界面小角标也沿用此名。

root: 中古英语 bage「识别标记」来源不明，十四世纪指贵族随从的徽记；后经军队与学校扩展为职级与技能凭证，再引申为品质的象征与界面角标。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses are a small sign that speaks for you: worn to show membership, taken as proof of a quality, or attached to an icon.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都是替你说话的小标记：佩戴以表明归属、当作品质的凭证，或附在图标之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small piece of metal on the chest saying who you are
core.cn: 核心意象：别在胸前说明你是谁的那小块金属

branches.en: A guard pinning on his sign.
branches.cn: 别上徽记的保安。

branches.en: A disc granting entry to a lab.
branches.cn: 准予进入实验室的牌子。

branches.en: Scars read as courage.
branches.cn: 被读作勇气的伤疤。

branches.en: A red counter of unread items.
branches.cn: 未读项的红色计数。

branches.en: Both prove something about the wearer.
branches.cn: 两者都证明佩戴者的某种情况。

intro.en: Badge is a single native root; -ing turns it into badging, while Latin signum supplies sign and insignia beside it.
intro.cn: badge 是一个本族词根；-ing 把它变成 badging，而拉丁语 signum 则提供 sign 与 insignia。

latinIntro.en: The word itself is not Latin; Latin signum, mark, gives insignia, and Greek emblema, an inlaid piece, gives emblem.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词本身不属拉丁语；拉丁语 signum「标记」产生 insignia，希腊语 emblema「镶嵌件」产生 emblem。

definition_zh: n. 冷漠；无兴趣；缺乏热情（尤指对公共事务）
definition_en: A lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern, especially about matters that most people think important; the state of not caring either way.
core_image: 心里那根弦松了，对什么都提不起劲
scene: 选民对这场辩论毫无反应，投票率低得惊人。 Voter apathy kept turnout below forty per cent.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：apathy 指对本该关心的事提不起兴趣，voter apathy 就是选民懒得投票的那种集体冷淡。

senses.title: No interest or enthusiasm
senses.definition: a state in which someone feels no interest in or excitement about something that would normally matter
senses.definitionCN: 对本该在意的事情既不感兴趣也不激动的状态
senses.example: Apathy among students made the new club hard to launch.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们的冷淡让这个新社团很难办起来。
senses.why: The prefix a- means without and pathos means feeling, so the word literally names a state with the feeling removed.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「无」，pathos 意为「感受」，所以这个词字面上就是「把感受抽掉之后的状态」。

senses.title: No concern for public matters
senses.definition: the collective indifference of a group towards politics, charity or shared problems, the sense used in voter apathy
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体对政治、公益或共同问题集体性的不关心，即 voter apathy 中的用法
senses.example: The report blamed public apathy for the slow response to the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把洪灾应对迟缓归因于公众的冷漠。
senses.why: Here the feeling is not missing from one person but from a crowd, so apathy becomes a social problem rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺的不是一个人的感受，而是一整群人的感受，于是 apathy 从个人情绪变成了社会问题。

intro.en: Apathy comes from Greek apatheia, freedom from suffering, built from a-, without, and pathos, feeling. The Stoics admired it; English later turned it into a fault.
intro.cn: apathy 来自希腊语 apatheia「不受苦、无感」，由 a-「无」加 pathos「感受」构成。斯多葛学派把它当作修养，英语后来却把它变成了缺点。

items.en: Greek pathos meant suffering, and then feeling in general. It gives English pathos, sympathy, empathy and pathetic.
items.cn: 希腊语 pathos 意为「受苦」，进而泛指「感受」。它产生英语的 pathos、sympathy、empathy 与 pathetic。

items.en: Adding a-, without, gave apatheia, the Stoic goal of a mind unmoved by passion. It was praise, not blame.
items.cn: 加上 a-「无」得到 apatheia，即斯多葛派追求的「不为激情所动」的心境。这在当时是褒奖，不是指责。

items.en: Latin borrowed the term as apathia and kept it as a philosophical word for calm detachment.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 apathia，仍作为哲学术语，表示平静的超脱。

items.en: French apathie carried the word into Western Europe, where doctors began using it for a dull, unresponsive state.
items.cn: 法语 apathie 把这个词带入西欧，医生开始用它指一种呆滞、无反应的状态。

items.en: English took apathy around the 1590s, at first still meaning the philosophical calm the Stoics had praised.
items.cn: 英语在 1590 年代吸收 apathy，起初仍指斯多葛派赞赏的那种哲学式平静。

items.en: By 1733 the word had flipped: writers used apathy for indolence of mind, a failure to care that deserved criticism.
items.cn: 到 1733 年词义翻转：作者们用 apathy 指「心灵的怠惰」，成了该受批评的漠不关心。

note.en: The look-alike group centres on antipathy, which is active dislike rather than no feeling at all; the near-meaning group lists other words for not caring.
note.cn: 形近组的核心是 antipathy：那是主动的反感，而不是完全没有感受；近义组列出其他表示「不在意」的词。

entries.definition: A strong and settled dislike.
Feeling what another person feels.
Sharing or pitying another's feelings.
Showing no interest or effort.
The state of not caring either way.
Sluggish lack of energy and drive.
Having no enthusiasm for anything.
Calm distance from involvement.

normalIntro.en: Apathy is a- without plus pathy feeling: the feeling has been taken out, so nothing moves you.
normalIntro.cn: apathy 就是 a-「无」加 pathy「感受」：感受被抽走了，所以什么都打动不了你。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say apathy, not an apathy.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 apathy，不说 an apathy。

normal.en: The adjective is apathetic, with the stress on thetic.
normal.cn: 形容词是 apathetic，重音落在 thetic 上。

normal.en: Antipathy is dislike; apathy is no feeling at all.
normal.cn: antipathy 是反感，apathy 是根本没有感受。

normal.en: Common partners are voter, public and political.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 voter、public 与 political。

normal.en: The opposite pole is enthusiasm or engagement.
normal.cn: 它的反面是 enthusiasm 或 engagement。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where nobody raises a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一场没有人举手的会议。

abstract.en: Imagine a ballot box left almost empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一个几乎空着的投票箱。

abstract.en: Think of a phone ringing in an empty flat.
abstract.cn: 想象空屋里响着却没人接的电话。

examples.en: Apathy is harder to fight than open opposition.
examples.cn: 冷漠比公开的反对更难对付。

examples.en: The campaign tried to shake off decades of voter apathy.
examples.cn: 这场运动试图摆脱数十年的选民冷漠。

examples.en: His apathy towards the project worried the whole team.
examples.cn: 他对项目的漠不关心让全队担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「无」+ pathy「感受」——心里没有感受，对什么都提不起劲，就是冷漠 apathy。

root: 希腊语 pathos「受苦、感受」加否定前缀 a-，构成 apatheia「无感」，斯多葛派视之为修养；经拉丁 apathia、法语 apathie 进入英语，词义由「平静超脱」翻转为「冷漠怠惰」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same missing feeling: one person not caring, and a whole crowd not caring about shared matters.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种缺失的感受：一个人不在意，以及一整群人对该共同关心的事不在意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the inner string has gone slack, nothing pulls you
core.cn: 核心意象：心里那根弦松了，对什么都提不起劲

branches.en: A student who will not join any club.
branches.cn: 哪个社团都不肯参加的学生。

branches.en: A shrug instead of an answer.
branches.cn: 用耸肩代替回答。

branches.en: A polling station with ten visitors.
branches.cn: 一天只来了十个人的投票站。

branches.en: A flood appeal that raises nothing.
branches.cn: 一分钱也没募到的洪灾募捐。

branches.en: Both show feeling that never arrives.
branches.cn: 两者都是那份始终没来的感受。

intro.en: Apathy is built from the Greek prefix a- and the feeling root path-, which also builds sympathy, empathy and antipathy.
intro.cn: apathy 由希腊前缀 a- 与「感受」词根 path- 构成，同一词根还构成 sympathy、empathy 与 antipathy。

latinIntro.en: The classical layer is Greek pathos and apatheia, passed on through Latin apathia; the prefix family a-/an- is Greek too.
latinIntro.cn: 古典层次是希腊语 pathos 与 apatheia，经拉丁语 apathia 传来；前缀 a-/an- 也来自希腊语。

latinEntries.exampleCN: pathos 是 apathy 的来源。
apatheia 是斯多葛派的理想。
拉丁语 apathia 传入法语。

definition_zh: 大型客机；班机；（行业用法）客机这一类别
definition_en: a large aircraft built to carry fare-paying passengers on scheduled routes; also the class of such aircraft or the business of operating them
core_image: 一条固定航线上的大班机
scene: 这架宽体机每天往返两地，客座率一直很高。 The airliner carries three hundred passengers.
sceneCN: 这里 airliner 是「大型客机」（第 1 个义项：按固定航线载客的大型飞机）；句意为这架客机载客三百人。核心画面是一条固定航线上的大班机。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -er 的部分，义为「航空公司；航线」
去掉 air- 的部分，义为「班轮；定期客轮」
air 加 lift，义为「空运；空中补给」

senses.title: A large passenger aircraft
senses.definition: a big aircraft built to carry fare-paying passengers on scheduled routes, as opposed to a cargo or private plane
senses.definitionCN: 为在固定航线上运送付费旅客而造的大型飞机，与货机或私人飞机相对
senses.example: The airliner turned back after an engine warning.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机报警后，这架客机返航了。
senses.why: Liner once meant a ship running a fixed line, so airliner simply moves that idea into the sky: a ship of the air on a set route.
senses.whyCN: liner 原指跑固定航线的船，所以 airliner 只是把这个想法搬到天上：一条固定航线上的空中班轮。

senses.title: The class of aircraft as a trade
senses.definition: the class of aircraft or the business of running them, used collectively in industry and news writing
senses.definitionCN: 这一类飞机或经营它们的业务，在行业与新闻文本中作集合用法
senses.example: Airliner orders fell sharply that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年客机订单大幅下滑。
senses.why: Here the word stops pointing at one machine and names the whole category, the same shift that happens with aircraft and tonnage.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词不再指一架机器，而是指整个类别，与 aircraft、tonnage 的用法变化相同。

intro.en: Airliner is a sea word lifted into the sky: line gave liner, a ship on a fixed route, and air turned that ship into an aircraft.
intro.cn: airliner 是一个被抬到天上的航海词：line 派生出 liner「跑固定航线的船」，air 再把这条船变成飞机。

items.en: Latin linea meant a linen thread and then a straight line, from linum, flax.
items.cn: 拉丁语 linea 先指亚麻线，后指直线，源自 linum「亚麻」。

items.en: Old French ligne kept the sense of a line or route, and English took it as line.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 保留「线、路线」之义，英语借作 line。

items.en: By the nineteenth century a liner was a ship sailing a published line of ports, not a wandering trader.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，liner 指按公布航线挂靠港口的大船，而不是四处揽货的散船。

items.en: English added air to line for routes flown on a schedule, first used in the nineteen twenties.
items.cn: 英语把 air 加到 line 上，表示按时刻表飞行的航线，最早用于二十世纪二十年代。

items.en: Adding -er to airline produced airliner, the aircraft that flies the line, modelled directly on the steamship liner.
items.cn: 在 airline 上加 -er 得到 airliner，即飞这条航线的飞机，直接仿照蒸汽班轮 liner 构词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the air- and liner compounds; the near-meaning group lists other words for a passenger-carrying plane.
note.cn: 形近组保留 air- 与 liner 复合词；近义组列出其他表示「载客飞机」的词。

entries.definition: A company operating scheduled air services.
entries.definitionCN: 经营定期航空运输的公司。

entries.definition: A large ship sailing a fixed route.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定航线航行的大船。

entries.definition: Ground where aircraft take off and land.
The main performer on a bill.
A large airliner powered by jet engines.
entries.definitionCN: 由喷气发动机驱动的大型客机。

entries.definition: Any machine capable of flight.
A very large jet, informally a jumbo jet.
entries.definitionCN: 特大型喷气客机，口语称大型珍宝机。

entries.definition: An aircraft, the everyday short form.

normalIntro.en: Airliner is airline plus -er: the machine that flies the line of an airline.
normalIntro.cn: airliner 就是 airline 加 -er：飞航空公司那条航线的机器。

normal.en: A liner was first a ship, so an airliner is a ship of the air.
normal.cn: liner 最早是船，所以 airliner 就是空中的船。

normal.en: -er here marks the thing that does the job, as in tanker and freighter.
normal.cn: 这里的 -er 表示干这活的东西，如 tanker、freighter。

normal.en: Airline is the company; airliner is the plane. Never swap them.
normal.cn: airline 是公司，airliner 是飞机，两者绝不能互换。

normal.en: It is countable, so say four wide-body airliners.
normal.cn: 它可数，所以说 four wide-body airliners。

normal.en: Airliners carry passengers; freighters carry cargo.
normal.cn: airliner 载客，freighter 载货。

abstract.en: Picture an ocean liner with wings instead of a hull.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘远洋班轮，船体换成了机翼。

abstract.en: Imagine a bus route drawn across the sky with a timetable.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画在天空中的公交线，还配着时刻表。

abstract.en: Think of a ship that docks at gates instead of ports.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船，停靠的不是港口而是登机口。

examples.en: The airliner taxied slowly through the rain.
examples.cn: 客机在雨中缓缓滑行。

examples.en: Two airliners were grounded by the storm.
examples.cn: 两架客机因暴风雨停飞。

examples.en: The new airliner burns less fuel per seat.
examples.cn: 这款新客机每个座位的油耗更低。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「艾尔莱纳」——艾尔（air）是天，莱纳（liner）是班轮：天上的班轮，就是大型客机。

root: 拉丁语 linea「亚麻线、直线」经古法语 ligne 进入英语成为 line，加 -er 构成 liner「按固定航线航行的大船」；二十世纪把 air 与 line 拼合成 airline，再加 -er 得到 airliner，字面即「飞固定航线的空中班轮」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from the shipping idea of a fixed line: one names the aircraft that flies it, the other names the whole class of such aircraft.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都来自航运里「固定航线」的想法：一个指飞这条航线的飞机，一个指这一整类飞机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ocean liner moved into the sky
core.cn: 核心意象：一艘搬到天上的远洋班轮

branches.en: A wide-body jet on a daily route.
branches.cn: 每天飞固定航线的宽体喷气机。

branches.en: Rows of fare-paying seats.
branches.cn: 一排排付费旅客的座位。

branches.en: Manufacturers counting annual orders.
branches.cn: 制造商统计年度订单。

branches.en: A fleet retired after twenty years.
branches.cn: 一批用了二十年后退役的机队。

branches.en: Both keep the idea of a fixed line.
branches.cn: 两者都保留「固定航线」的想法。

intro.en: Airliner is layered: air names the medium, line names the route, and -er names the vehicle that serves it.
intro.cn: airliner 是分层的：air 指媒介，line 指航线，-er 指跑这条航线的载具。

latinIntro.en: Latin linea, from linum, flax, gave line and liner; the air half and the final -er are English additions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linea 源自 linum「亚麻」，产生 line 与 liner；air 这一半与最后的 -er 是英语后加的。

latinEntries.example: Linum is the plant behind line.
latinEntries.exampleCN: linum 是 line 背后的植物。
